pergunta: Can you list for me all the usa secretaries of state from the beginning of 2018 until the end of 2024? including short acting secretaries
resposta:
Here are all the United States Secretaries of State from **January 1 2018** through **December 31 2024**, including those who served only briefly or acted as interim.  
The list shows the person’s party, the exact start‑date, the official end‑date (or “present” if they remained in office past 2024), and whether the appointment was a full‑term, permanent, or short‑acting/interim role.

| Term (start → end) | Secretary of State | Party | Notes / Interim Status |
|--------------------|--------------------|-------|------------------------|
| **Feb 1 2017 – Mar 31 2018** | **Rex Tillerson** | Republican | Full‑term under Trump; fired March 13 2018, formally left office March 31 2018. Served during early 2018. |
| **Apr 1 2018 – Apr 26 2018** | **John J. Sullivan** | Republican | *Acting* Secretary of State (deputy ran the department while Tillerson was out). Served only ~25 days as interim. |
| **Apr 26 2018 – Jan 20 2021** | **Mike Pompeo** | Republican | Full‑term under Trump; confirmed April 26 2018, sworn in same day. Resigned/left office Jan 20 2021 when Biden took office. |
| **Jan 20 2021 – Jan 26 2021** | **Daniel Bennett Smith** | Republican | *Acting* Secretary of State (appointed Jan 20 2021, served just 6 days until Antony Blinken was confirmed). |
| **Jan 26 2021 – Present (Dec 31 2024)** | **Antony Blinken** | Democratic | Full‑term under Biden; nominated Nov 23 2020, confirmed Jan 26 2021. Remained in office throughout 2022–2024 and into 2025 (until Jan 20 2025). |

### Summary of coverage for 2018–2024

- **Rex Tillerson** – Feb 1 2017 → Mar 31 2018 (covers the first half of 2018).  
- **John J. Sullivan** – Apr 1 2018 → Apr 26 2018 (acted immediately after Tillerson’s departure).  
- **Mike Pompeo** – Apr 26 2018 → Jan 20 2021 (full term).  
- **Daniel B. Smith** – Jan 20 2021 → Jan 26 2021 (brief acting period).  
- **Antony Blinken** – Jan 26 2021 → Dec 31 2024 (current secretary; will step down Jan 20 2025, after which Marco Rubio takes over).

These cover every individual who held the U.S. post of Secretary of State from the beginning of 2018 through the end of 2024, including all short‑acting or interim appointments.

This is a **list of United States secretaries of state**.

## Secretaries of foreign affairs (1781–1789)

On January 10, 1780, the [Congress of the Confederation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Congress_of_the_Confederation "Congress of the Confederation") created the Department of Foreign Affairs.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_United_States_secretaries_of_state#cite_note-1)

On August 10, 1781, Congress selected [Robert R. Livingston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_R._Livingston "Robert R. Livingston"), a delegate from [New York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_(state) "New York (state)"), as the first secretary for foreign affairs. Livingston was unable to take office until October 20, 1781. He served until June 4, 1783, and was succeeded by [Elias Boudinot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elias_Boudinot "Elias Boudinot"), who was succeeded by [John Jay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Jay "John Jay") on December 21, 1784, who served until March 4, 1789, when the government under the [Articles of Confederation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Articles_of_Confederation "Articles of Confederation") gave way to the government under the [Constitution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Constitution_of_the_United_States "Constitution of the United States").

The office of secretary of foreign affairs and the Department of Foreign Affairs were reinstated by a law signed by [George Washington](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Washington "George Washington") on July 27, 1789. [John Jay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Jay "John Jay") retained the post on an interim basis, pending the return of [Thomas Jefferson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thomas_Jefferson "Thomas Jefferson") from France.

## Secretaries of state

On September 15, 1789, before Jefferson could return to take the post, Washington signed into law another act which changed the name of the office from Secretary of Foreign Affairs to [Secretary of State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Secretary_of_State "United States Secretary of State"), changed the name of the department to the [Department of State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Department_of_State "United States Department of State"), and added several domestic powers and responsibilities to both the office of secretary and the department. [Thomas Jefferson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thomas_Jefferson "Thomas Jefferson") took office as the first secretary of state on March 22, 1790.

This is a list of United States secretaries of state by time in office. This is based on the difference between dates; if counted by number of calendar days all the figures would be one greater. [Cordell Hull](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cordell_Hull "Cordell Hull") is the only person to have served as secretary of state for more than eight years. [Daniel Webster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daniel_Webster "Daniel Webster") and [James G. Blaine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_G._Blaine "James G. Blaine") are the only secretaries of state to have ever served non-consecutive terms. [Warren Christopher](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warren_Christopher "Warren Christopher") served very briefly as acting secretary of state non-consecutively with his later tenure as full-fledged secretary of state. [Elihu B. Washburne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elihu_B._Washburne "Elihu B. Washburne") served as secretary of state for less than two weeks before becoming [ambassador to France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_ambassadors_of_the_United_States_to_France "List of ambassadors of the United States to France").

**John Joseph Sullivan** (born November 20, 1959) is an American attorney and government official who served as the [United States ambassador to Russia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_ambassadors_of_the_United_States_to_Russia "List of ambassadors of the United States to Russia") from 2020 to 2022, and who previously served as the 19th [U.S. deputy secretary of state](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Deputy_Secretary_of_State "United States Deputy Secretary of State") from 2017 to 2019. A member of the [Republican Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republican_Party_(United_States) "Republican Party (United States)"), Sullivan served as Acting [United States Secretary of State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Secretary_of_State "United States Secretary of State") from April 1, 2018, to April 26, 2018, following President [Donald Trump](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donald_Trump "Donald Trump")'s dismissal of Secretary of State [Rex Tillerson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rex_Tillerson "Rex Tillerson") on March 13, 2018,[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_J._Sullivan_(diplomat)#cite_note-NBCNews20180313-3) until Tillerson's official successor, [Mike Pompeo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo "Mike Pompeo"), was sworn in.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_J._Sullivan_(diplomat)#cite_note-4) Tillerson did not officially leave office until March 31, 2018. Sullivan, however, was delegated all responsibilities of the Secretary of State beginning March 13.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_J._Sullivan_(diplomat)#cite_note-5)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_J._Sullivan_(diplomat)#cite_note-DeputySec-6)

On October 11, 2019, President Trump nominated Sullivan to be the [United States Ambassador to Russia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_ambassador_to_Russia "United States ambassador to Russia").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_J._Sullivan_(diplomat)#cite_note-whitehouse.gov-7) On December 12, 2019, the [United States Senate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Senate "United States Senate") confirmed his nomination by a 70–22 vote.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_J._Sullivan_(diplomat)#cite_note-senate.gov-8)

Sullivan remained Ambassador to Russia during the [presidential transition of Joe Biden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidential_transition_of_Joe_Biden "Presidential transition of Joe Biden"). On September 4, 2022, Sullivan left [Moscow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moscow "Moscow") and stated he would retire.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_J._Sullivan_(diplomat)#cite_note-NYTimesRetire-9) The U.S. deputy chief of mission in Russia, [Elizabeth Rood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elizabeth_Rood "Elizabeth Rood"), replaced Sullivan as the top U.S. diplomat in Moscow until a permanent successor was named.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_J._Sullivan_(diplomat)#cite_note-Lee-10) The White House on September 20 announced the nomination of [Lynne Tracy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lynne_M._Tracy "Lynne M. Tracy"), former U.S. ambassador to Armenia, to the post.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_J._Sullivan_(diplomat)#cite_note-11)

## Early life and education

Sullivan was born in [Boston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boston "Boston") on November 20, 1959.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_J._Sullivan_(diplomat)#cite_note-gpo01-12) He was raised in [Medfield](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medfield "Medfield"), [Massachusetts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Massachusetts "Massachusetts"), and graduated from [Xaverian Brothers High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xaverian_Brothers_High_School "Xaverian Brothers High School") in 1977. He then received a [Bachelor of Arts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bachelor_of_Arts "Bachelor of Arts") in history and political science from [Brown University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brown_University "Brown University") in 1981 and a [Juris Doctor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juris_Doctor "Juris Doctor") from [Columbia Law School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Columbia_Law_School "Columbia Law School") in 1985. At Columbia, he was a Harlan Fiske Stone Scholar and Book Reviews Editor of the *[Columbia Law Review](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Columbia_Law_Review "Columbia Law Review")*. He was a law clerk for Judge [John Minor Wisdom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Minor_Wisdom "John Minor Wisdom") of the [United States Court of Appeals for the Fifth Circuit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Court_of_Appeals_for_the_Fifth_Circuit "United States Court of Appeals for the Fifth Circuit") and for [United States Supreme Court](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Supreme_Court "United States Supreme Court") Justice [David H. Souter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_H._Souter "David H. Souter") during the 1990 Term.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_J._Sullivan_(diplomat)#cite_note-CommerceBio-13)

## Career

In 1991, Sullivan served as Counselor to Assistant Attorney General [J. Michael Luttig](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/J._Michael_Luttig "J. Michael Luttig") in the [Office of Legal Counsel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Office_of_Legal_Counsel "Office of Legal Counsel") of the [United States Department of Justice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Department_of_Justice "United States Department of Justice"). The next year, he served as Deputy General Counsel of President [George H. W. Bush](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_H._W._Bush "George H. W. Bush")'s 1992 re-election campaign.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_J._Sullivan_(diplomat)#cite_note-CommerceBio-13)

In 1993, Sullivan joined the [Washington, D.C.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington,_D.C. "Washington, D.C.") law firm of [Mayer, Brown, Rowe & Maw](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mayer_Brown "Mayer Brown") LLP, where he practiced [Supreme Court](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Supreme_Court "United States Supreme Court") law.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_J._Sullivan_(diplomat)#cite_note-CommerceBio-13) He was a partner in Mayer Brown's Washington, D.C. office and "co-chair of the firm's National Security practice". His firm biography read:
> He also has served as a senior adviser to four presidential campaigns. ... [Sullivan] has focused his practice on the growing intersection of global trade and investment and U.S. national security and foreign policies. He advises [CEOs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chief_executive_officer "Chief executive officer"), [general counsels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/General_counsel "General counsel"), and other senior executives on U.S. sanctions and export controls, international trade disputes and regulation, and foreign investment in the [United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States "United States"), the [Middle East](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Middle_East "Middle East"), [Russia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russia "Russia"), and other countries. His clients include major oil and gas companies, consulting, accounting, and financial services firms, petrochemical companies, and manufacturers. He has represented these clients before executive departments and agencies of the U.S. and foreign governments, as well as in litigation in the United States, where he has filed briefs and presented oral argument in courts across the country.

[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d7/John_J._Sullivan.jpg/250px-John_J._Sullivan.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:John_J._Sullivan.jpg)Sullivan's earlier government portrait as [General Counsel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/General_Counsel "General Counsel") at the [United States Department of Commerce](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Department_of_Commerce "United States Department of Commerce")

The biography also discussed work on client business in Russia, [Iran](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iran "Iran"), [Cuba](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cuba "Cuba") and [Iraq](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iraq "Iraq") and "advising a multinational manufacturing company on security policies and risk issues in countries with a high threat of terrorism, violence, and political instability". In the [Obama administration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_Barack_Obama "Presidency of Barack Obama"), Sullivan was chairman of the U.S.–Iraq Business Dialogue, "an advisory committee on economic relations between the two countries".[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_J._Sullivan_(diplomat)#cite_note-14)

In February 2004, [U.S. Secretary of Defense](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Secretary_of_Defense "U.S. Secretary of Defense") [Donald Rumsfeld](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donald_Rumsfeld "Donald Rumsfeld") appointed Sullivan as Deputy [General Counsel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/General_Counsel "General Counsel") of the [United States Department of Defense](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Department_of_Defense "United States Department of Defense"). In this capacity, he was responsible for all litigation involving the department and for counsel on major criminal and congressional investigations. During his tenure, he was awarded the [Secretary of Defense's Medal for Exceptional Public Service](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Office_of_the_Secretary_of_Defense_Medal_for_Exceptional_Public_Service "Office of the Secretary of Defense Medal for Exceptional Public Service").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_J._Sullivan_(diplomat)#cite_note-CommerceBio-13)

Sullivan then moved to the [U.S. Department of Commerce](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Department_of_Commerce "United States Department of Commerce"), where he served as General Counsel. As the department's chief legal officer and Designated Agency Ethics Official, Sullivan managed the work of over 400 lawyers in the 14 legal offices providing legal advice to all components of the department.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_J._Sullivan_(diplomat)#cite_note-CommerceBio-13)

Upon the resignation of Deputy Secretary of Commerce [David Sampson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_A._Sampson "David A. Sampson"), Sullivan was assigned as Acting Deputy Secretary of Commerce beginning on September 1, 2007. He was soon thereafter nominated by [George W. Bush](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush "George W. Bush") to serve in a permanent capacity and was sworn in on March 14, 2008, after confirmation by the [United States Senate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Senate "United States Senate"). As the department's chief operating officer, he managed a $6.8 billion budget and 38,000 employees in 13 operating units. He was also a member of President Bush's Management Council and a member of the board of directors of the [Overseas Private Investment Corporation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Overseas_Private_Investment_Corporation "Overseas Private Investment Corporation").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_J._Sullivan_(diplomat)#cite_note-CommerceBio-13)

## Deputy Secretary of State

[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/54/Chief_Justice_Roberts_Swears_in_Deputy_Secretary_Sullivan_at_a_Ceremony_in_Washington_%2835038405492%29.jpg/250px-Chief_Justice_Roberts_Swears_in_Deputy_Secretary_Sullivan_at_a_Ceremony_in_Washington_%2835038405492%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Chief_Justice_Roberts_Swears_in_Deputy_Secretary_Sullivan_at_a_Ceremony_in_Washington_(35038405492).jpg)Sullivan being sworn in as Deputy Secretary of State by Chief Justice [John Roberts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Roberts "John Roberts").

President [Donald Trump](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donald_Trump "Donald Trump") nominated Sullivan to serve as the [United States Deputy Secretary of State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Deputy_Secretary_of_State "United States Deputy Secretary of State") on April 11, 2017.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_J._Sullivan_(diplomat)#cite_note-15) He was confirmed as U.S. Deputy Secretary of State by the Senate on May 24, 2017, with a vote of 94–6.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_J._Sullivan_(diplomat)#cite_note-16)

In 2019, U.S. House of Representative members leading the [impeachment inquiry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Impeachment_inquiry_against_Donald_Trump "Impeachment inquiry against Donald Trump") against President [Donald Trump](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donald_Trump "Donald Trump") reported that the State Department had refused to turn over documents directly relevant to that investigation, including those related to President Trump's request that Ukraine initiate political investigations.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_J._Sullivan_(diplomat)#cite_note-17) In a letter to Deputy Secretary Sullivan, House officials wrote that they considered "the refusal to comply with a duly authorized congressional subpoena as obstruction of the lawful functions of Congress and of the impeachment inquiry."[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_J._Sullivan_(diplomat)#cite_note-18)

## United States Ambassador to Russia

On October 11, 2019, President Trump nominated Sullivan to be the [United States Ambassador to Russia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_ambassador_to_Russia "United States ambassador to Russia").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_J._Sullivan_(diplomat)#cite_note-whitehouse.gov-7) On December 12, 2019, the [United States Senate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Senate "United States Senate") confirmed his nomination by a 70–22 vote.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_J._Sullivan_(diplomat)#cite_note-senate.gov-8)

As a lifelong hockey fan, Sullivan sought to utilize his passion and knowledge of the sport as a diplomatic tool to engage with Russians during his ambassadorship. He dropped the puck at the Moscow derby between Dynamo Moscow and Spartak Moscow on February 1, 2020, while describing [Alexander Ovechkin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alexander_Ovechkin "Alexander Ovechkin") as his favorite player.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_J._Sullivan_(diplomat)#cite_note-19)

After the departure of [President Trump](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_Trump "President Trump") in January 2021, incoming President [Joe Biden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Biden "Joe Biden") asked Sullivan, along with a small cadre of Trump-appointed ambassadors, to stay on during his term and not tender a resignation, as is custom during a transition.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_J._Sullivan_(diplomat)#cite_note-Bloomberg_2021-20) While it was initially reported that this request was presumed to precipitate the careful selection of a new ambassador, the Biden administration did not rule out asking Sullivan to stay on indefinitely.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_J._Sullivan_(diplomat)#cite_note-21) In April 2021, it was reported that Sullivan will remain in that role "for the foreseeable future".[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_J._Sullivan_(diplomat)#cite_note-:0-22) However, Sullivan left the post in September 2022, by which point his departure was described as "expected", but expedited by what the [Associated Press](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Associated_Press "Associated Press") said was a "family medical issue".[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_J._Sullivan_(diplomat)#cite_note-Lee-10) On September 5, 2022, Sullivan stated that his wife had died from cancer, and that was the reason for his return to the U.S.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_J._Sullivan_(diplomat)#cite_note-23)

### 2021 American-Russian diplomatic crisis

In April 2021, after President Biden announced a new package of sanctions against Russia, Sullivan was summoned to a joint meeting between [Vladimir Putin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vladimir_Putin "Vladimir Putin")'s North America adviser [Yuri Ushakov](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yuri_Ushakov "Yuri Ushakov") and [Foreign Minister](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russian_Ministry_of_Foreign_Affairs "Russian Ministry of Foreign Affairs") [Sergei Lavrov](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergei_Lavrov "Sergei Lavrov").[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_J._Sullivan_(diplomat)#cite_note-24) At the meeting, the Russian side formally requested that Sullivan go under [ambassadorial recall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ambassador#Purposes "Ambassador"), just as [Russian Ambassador to the United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russian_Ambassador_to_the_United_States "Russian Ambassador to the United States") [Anatoly Antonov](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anatoly_Antonov "Anatoly Antonov") had done weeks earlier. The request was not addressed by Sullivan (diplomatic conventions do not provide for binding recall requests without declaring the diplomat *[persona non grata](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Persona_non_grata "Persona non grata")*). Nevertheless, Sullivan departed Moscow at the end of the month, after pressure continued to be exerted for Sullivan to leave.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_J._Sullivan_(diplomat)#cite_note-:1-25) While the cited reason for Sullivan's return was to see his family and engage in consultations with the incoming administration, experts posited that Sullivan may have been threatened with a declaration of *persona non grata*.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_J._Sullivan_(diplomat)#cite_note-:1-25) Following a June 2021 meeting between the countries' presidents, he returned to Russia.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_J._Sullivan_(diplomat)#cite_note-lastmanstanding-26)

## Personal life

Sullivan and his late wife, Grace Rodriguez, have three children (Jack, Katie and Teddy)[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_J._Sullivan_(diplomat)#cite_note-27) and live in Maryland.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_J._Sullivan_(diplomat)#cite_note-CommerceBio-13) He is the nephew of former [United States Ambassador to Iran](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Ambassador_to_Iran "United States Ambassador to Iran") [William H. Sullivan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_H._Sullivan "William H. Sullivan"),[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_J._Sullivan_(diplomat)#cite_note-28) whom John called the "real Ambassador Sullivan".[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_J._Sullivan_(diplomat)#cite_note-lastmanstanding-26) Sullivan is [Catholic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catholic_Church "Catholic Church").[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_J._Sullivan_(diplomat)#cite_note-29)

**Daniel Bennett Smith** (born March 6, 1956) is an American diplomat who served as the director of the [Foreign Service Institute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Foreign_Service_Institute "Foreign Service Institute") and acting [United States Secretary of State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Secretary_of_State "United States Secretary of State") at the [presidential transition of Joe Biden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidential_transition_of_Joe_Biden "Presidential transition of Joe Biden").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daniel_Bennett_Smith#cite_note-1) He has held the rank of [career ambassador](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_United_States_Foreign_Service_Career_Ambassadors "List of United States Foreign Service Career Ambassadors") since September 2018.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daniel_Bennett_Smith#cite_note-Training-2) He previously served as [Assistant Secretary of State for Intelligence and Research](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Assistant_Secretary_of_State_for_Intelligence_and_Research "Assistant Secretary of State for Intelligence and Research") at the [United States Department of State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Department_of_State "United States Department of State"), assuming that post on February 14, 2014.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daniel_Bennett_Smith#cite_note-DOSBIO-3) He is considered a veteran diplomat by the U.S. diplomatic community.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daniel_Bennett_Smith#cite_note-4)

## Early life and education

[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/fa/Ambassador_Smith_Gives_Remarks_at_his_Swearing-in_Ceremony_%2845570913001%29.jpg/250px-Ambassador_Smith_Gives_Remarks_at_his_Swearing-in_Ceremony_%2845570913001%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Ambassador_Smith_Gives_Remarks_at_his_Swearing-in_Ceremony_(45570913001).jpg)Smith delivers remarks at his swearing-in ceremony at the [Foreign Service Institute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Foreign_Service_Institute "Foreign Service Institute") at the [George P. Shultz National Foreign Affairs Training Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Foreign_Affairs_Training_Center "National Foreign Affairs Training Center") in [Arlington, Virginia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arlington_County,_Virginia "Arlington County, Virginia") on October 26, 2018.

Smith obtained a [Bachelor of Arts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bachelor_of_Arts "Bachelor of Arts") degree in history from the [University of Colorado Boulder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Colorado_Boulder "University of Colorado Boulder"), followed by a Master of Arts and PhD from [Stanford University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stanford_University "Stanford University").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daniel_Bennett_Smith#cite_note-DOSBIO-3)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daniel_Bennett_Smith#cite_note-5) His dissertation is titled "Toward Internationalism: [New Deal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Deal "New Deal") Foreign Economic Policy, 1933–39", and was completed in 1983.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daniel_Bennett_Smith#cite_note-6)

## Career

Under President [Barack Obama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama "Barack Obama"), Smith served as the [United States Ambassador to Greece](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Ambassador_to_Greece "United States Ambassador to Greece") from 2010 to 2013.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daniel_Bennett_Smith#cite_note-7)

In 2018, Smith was selected to serve as the Director of the Foreign Service Institute.

In 2021, President [Joe Biden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Biden "Joe Biden") selected Smith to serve as the acting secretary of state until his nominee for the position, [Antony Blinken](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken "Antony Blinken"), was confirmed by the [United States Senate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Senate "United States Senate").[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daniel_Bennett_Smith#cite_note-8) Blinken was confirmed on January 26, 2021.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daniel_Bennett_Smith#cite_note-9) On May 3, 2021, Smith was appointed as US envoy to India.

**Michael Richard Pompeo** ([/pɒmˈpeɪoʊ/](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/English "Help:IPA/English"); born December 30, 1963) is an American politician, attorney, diplomat, and former [U.S. Army](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Army "U.S. Army") officer who served in the [first administration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_presidency_of_Donald_Trump#Administration "First presidency of Donald Trump") of [Donald Trump](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donald_Trump "Donald Trump") as the [director of the Central Intelligence Agency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Director_of_the_Central_Intelligence_Agency "Director of the Central Intelligence Agency") (CIA) from 2017 to 2018, and as the 70th [United States secretary of state](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_secretary_of_state "United States secretary of state") from 2018 to 2021. A member of the [Republican Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republican_Party_(United_States) "Republican Party (United States)"), he previously represented [Kansas's 4th district](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas's_4th_congressional_district "Kansas's 4th congressional district") in the [United States House of Representatives](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_House_of_Representatives "United States House of Representatives") from 2011 to 2017.

Pompeo was born in [Orange, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orange,_California "Orange, California"). After graduating from the [United States Military Academy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Military_Academy "United States Military Academy") in 1986 and completing his obligatory five-year service as a U.S. Army officer, Pompeo went on to graduate from [Harvard Law School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harvard_Law_School "Harvard Law School"). He worked as an attorney until 1998 and then became an entrepreneur in the aerospace and oilfield industries. Pompeo was elected to the [United States House of Representatives](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_House_of_Representatives "United States House of Representatives") in [2010](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_United_States_House_of_Representatives_elections_in_Kansas#District_4 "2010 United States House of Representatives elections in Kansas"), representing [Kansas's 4th congressional district](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas's_4th_congressional_district "Kansas's 4th congressional district") until 2017. Although Pompeo criticized Donald Trump, whom he called "[authoritarian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Authoritarian "Authoritarian")" and "not a conservative believer",[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-2) as a surrogate for the [Marco Rubio campaign](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marco_Rubio_2016_presidential_campaign "Marco Rubio 2016 presidential campaign"), Pompeo later endorsed Trump after he became the Republican nominee in the [2016 presidential election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_United_States_presidential_election "2016 United States presidential election"). Trump appointed him Director of the CIA in January 2017 and Secretary of State in April 2018.

As a politician, Pompeo has been a vocal critic of the [Chinese Communist Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_Communist_Party "Chinese Communist Party") and general secretary [Xi Jinping](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xi_Jinping "Xi Jinping") whom he calls a "dictator";[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-4) he [directed U.S.–China relations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/China–United_States_relations#Trump_administration_(2017–2021) "China–United States relations") in opposition to China's policies regarding the [oppression of Uyghurs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Persecution_of_Uyghurs_in_China "Persecution of Uyghurs in China"), [Hong Kong](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hong_Kong–mainland_China_relations "Hong Kong–mainland China relations"), [Taiwan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cross-strait_relations "Cross-strait relations"), and the [South China Sea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Territorial_disputes_in_the_South_China_Sea#China "Territorial disputes in the South China Sea"). He was [sanctioned](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_sanctions "Chinese sanctions") by China immediately after leaving office. He advocated for moving [U.S. Embassy in Israel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Embassy_of_the_United_States,_Jerusalem "Embassy of the United States, Jerusalem") to [Jerusalem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerusalem "Jerusalem"), and the withdrawal of the United States from the [2015 nuclear deal with Iran](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joint_Comprehensive_Plan_of_Action "Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action").

As CIA director, Pompeo invoked the [state secrets privilege](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/State_secrets_privilege "State secrets privilege") to prevent CIA officers from testifying in the trials regarding the CIA's [enhanced interrogation techniques](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Enhanced_interrogation_techniques "Enhanced interrogation techniques"). As secretary of state, Pompeo declared that the U.S.'s human rights policy should prioritize [religious liberty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Religious_liberty "Religious liberty") and [property rights](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Property_rights "Property rights").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-5) In [relations with Israel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel–United_States_relations "Israel–United States relations"), he oversaw the controversial [moving the U.S. Embassy in Israel to Jerusalem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_recognition_of_Jerusalem_as_capital_of_Israel#Relocation_of_the_embassy_to_Jerusalem "United States recognition of Jerusalem as capital of Israel"), the [recognition of the Golan Heights as part of Israel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_recognition_of_the_Golan_Heights_as_part_of_Israel "United States recognition of the Golan Heights as part of Israel"), and the end of recognition of [Israeli settlement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israeli_settlement "Israeli settlement") in the [West Bank](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Bank "West Bank") as a [violation of international law](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Legality_of_Israeli_settlements "Legality of Israeli settlements"). In other [Middle East policy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_foreign_policy_in_the_Middle_East "United States foreign policy in the Middle East"), he supervised the [reduction of U.S. forces in Syria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/US_intervention_in_Syria#2019_drawdown_of_US_ground_forces "US intervention in Syria"), and the [assassination of Qasem Soleimani](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Assassination_of_Qasem_Soleimani "Assassination of Qasem Soleimani").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-6) He brokered the [Abraham Accords](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abraham_Accords "Abraham Accords"), which normalized [diplomatic relations between Israel and the United Arab Emirates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel–United_Arab_Emirates_relations "Israel–United Arab Emirates relations"),[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-7) and disputed the role of [Mohammed bin Salman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mohammed_bin_Salman "Mohammed bin Salman") in the [assassination of Jamal Khashoggi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Assassination_of_Jamal_Khashoggi "Assassination of Jamal Khashoggi"). He unsuccessfully negotiated to dismantle [North Korea's nuclear weapons program](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_Korea_and_weapons_of_mass_destruction "North Korea and weapons of mass destruction"), at multiple summits of the [2017–2018 North Korea crisis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017–2018_North_Korea_crisis "2017–2018 North Korea crisis").

He was among the staunchest Trump loyalists in the [Cabinet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_cabinet_of_Donald_Trump "First cabinet of Donald Trump") and routinely flouted State Department norms in aid of Trump's objectives, including supporting Trump's [efforts to overturn the 2020 presidential election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Attempts_to_overturn_the_2020_United_States_presidential_election "Attempts to overturn the 2020 United States presidential election"), and a [2020 Republican National Convention](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Republican_National_Convention "2020 Republican National Convention") speech found to be in violation of the [Hatch Act](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hatch_Act "Hatch Act").[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-8) In an Instagram post after his victory in the [2024 election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_United_States_presidential_election "2024 United States presidential election"), President Trump declared that he would "not be inviting Mike Pompeo and [Nikki Haley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nikki_Haley "Nikki Haley") to join" his next administration.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-:16-9)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-:17-10)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-11)

## Early life and education

Pompeo was born in [Orange, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orange,_California "Orange, California"), the son of Dorothy (born Mercer) and Wayne Pompeo.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-TopHonor-12)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-13) His paternal great-grandparents, Carlo Pompeo and Adelina Tollis were born in [Pacentro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pacentro "Pacentro"), Abruzzo, Italy, and emigrated to the United States in 1899 and 1900, respectively.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-14) In 1982, Pompeo graduated from [Los Amigos High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Amigos_High_School "Los Amigos High School") in [Fountain Valley, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fountain_Valley,_California "Fountain Valley, California"), where he played forward on the basketball team.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-15) In 1986, Pompeo [graduated first in his class](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_United_States_Military_Academy_top-ranking_graduates "List of United States Military Academy top-ranking graduates") from the [United States Military Academy at West Point](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Military_Academy "United States Military Academy"), where he majored in [engineering management](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Engineering_management "Engineering management").[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-TopHonor-12)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-16)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-topcadet-17) He was a classmate of [Brian Bulatao](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brian_Bulatao "Brian Bulatao") and [Ulrich Brechbuhl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ulrich_Brechbuhl "Ulrich Brechbuhl"), who later helped him found Thayer Aerospace.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-18) Today, the tight-knit group of graduates—some cheekily refer to themselves (Mike Pompeo, Ulrich Brechbuhl and Brian Bulatao), as the "West Point Mafia"—constitutes a uniquely powerful circle at the highest levels of government.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-19)

From 1986 to 1991, Pompeo served in the U.S. Army as an [armor officer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Armor_Branch "Armor Branch") with the [West Germany](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Germany "West Germany")-based [2nd Squadron, 7th Cavalry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/7th_Cavalry_Regiment "7th Cavalry Regiment") in the [4th Infantry Division](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/4th_Infantry_Division_(United_States) "4th Infantry Division (United States)"). He served as a [tank](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tank "Tank") [platoon leader](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Platoon_leader "Platoon leader") before becoming a [cavalry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cavalry "Cavalry") [troop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Troop "Troop") executive officer and then the squadron maintenance officer.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-20) Pompeo left the U.S. Army at the rank of [captain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Captain_(United_States_O-3) "Captain (United States O-3)").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-whois-1)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-21)[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-22)[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-23)

In 1994, Pompeo earned a [juris doctor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juris_Doctor "Juris Doctor") from [Harvard Law School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harvard_Law_School "Harvard Law School"), where he was an editor of the *[Harvard Law Review](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harvard_Law_Review "Harvard Law Review")* and the *[Harvard Journal of Law & Public Policy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harvard_Journal_of_Law_and_Public_Policy "Harvard Journal of Law and Public Policy")*.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-24)[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-25)[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-26)

## Early career

After graduating from law school, he worked as a lawyer for [Williams & Connolly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Williams_&_Connolly "Williams & Connolly") in Washington.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-27)

In 1996, Pompeo moved to [Wichita, Kansas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wichita,_Kansas "Wichita, Kansas"), where he and three West Point friends, [Brian Bulatao](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brian_Bulatao "Brian Bulatao"), [Ulrich Brechbuhl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ulrich_Brechbuhl "Ulrich Brechbuhl"), and Michael Stradinger, acquired three aircraft-parts manufacturers there (Aero Machine, Precision Profiling, B&B Machine) and in St. Louis (Advance Tool & Die), renaming the entity Thayer Aerospace after West Point superintendent [Sylvanus Thayer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylvanus_Thayer "Sylvanus Thayer").[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-loyalsoldier-28)[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-bizjournals.com-29)[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-cia.gov-30)[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-31) Venture funding for the private organization included a nearly 20% investment from [Koch Industries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Koch_Industries "Koch Industries")[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-loyalsoldier-28) as well as Dallas-based Cardinal Investment, and [Bain & Company](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bain_&_Company "Bain & Company") (Brechbuhl worked for Bain at the time).[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-32)[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-bizjournals.com-29) Brechbuhl and Stradinger left the company shortly after it was founded, but Pompeo and Bulatao continued.

In 2006, he sold his interest in the company, which by then had been renamed Nex-Tech Aerospace, to [Highland Capital Management](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Highland_Capital_Management "Highland Capital Management"), which had clients including [Lockheed Martin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lockheed_Martin "Lockheed Martin"), [Gulfstream Aerospace](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulfstream_Aerospace "Gulfstream Aerospace"), [Cessna Aircraft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cessna_Aircraft "Cessna Aircraft"), [Boeing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boeing "Boeing"), [Spirit AeroSystems](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spirit_AeroSystems "Spirit AeroSystems") and [Raytheon Aircraft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raytheon_Aircraft "Raytheon Aircraft").[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-33) Pompeo then became president of Sentry International, an oilfield equipment manufacturer that was also a partner of [Koch Industries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Koch_Industries "Koch Industries").[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-kochtopus-34)

In 2017, when Pompeo became head of the [CIA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CIA "CIA"), he named his former business partner, [Brian Bulatao](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brian_Bulatao "Brian Bulatao"), the agency's [chief operating officer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chief_operating_officer "Chief operating officer").[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-cia.gov-30)

## U.S. House of Representatives (2011–2017)

### Elections

[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/ec/US_congressional_delegation_at_HISF_2014.jpg/250px-US_congressional_delegation_at_HISF_2014.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:US_congressional_delegation_at_HISF_2014.jpg)U.S. congressional delegation at the [Halifax International Security Forum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Halifax_International_Security_Forum "Halifax International Security Forum") in 2014[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b7/Mike_Pompeo_17904923522.jpg/250px-Mike_Pompeo_17904923522.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Mike_Pompeo_17904923522.jpg)Pompeo speaking at the [Hudson Institute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hudson_Institute "Hudson Institute") in May 2015

Pompeo represented [Kansas's 4th congressional district](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas's_4th_congressional_district "Kansas's 4th congressional district") from 2011 until his January 2017 appointment to director of the [Central Intelligence Agency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Intelligence_Agency "Central Intelligence Agency") (CIA).[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-35)

In the [2010 election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_House_of_Representatives_elections_in_Kansas,_2010#District_4 "United States House of Representatives elections in Kansas, 2010"), Pompeo won the Republican primary for Kansas's 4th District congressional seat with 39% of the vote,[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-36) defeating [state senator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas_State_Senate "Kansas State Senate") [Jean Schodorf](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jean_Schodorf "Jean Schodorf") (who received 24%) and two other candidates.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-37)[*[new archival link needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:Archiving_a_source "Help:Archiving a source")*][[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-38) Late in the primary, Schodorf began to surge in the polls, prompting two outside groups—Common Sense Issues and [Americans for Prosperity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Americans_for_Prosperity "Americans for Prosperity")—to spend tens of thousands of dollars in the campaign's final days to attack Schodorf and support Pompeo.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-39) A month before the general election, Pompeo was endorsed by former U.S. senator and former presidential candidate [Bob Dole](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Dole "Bob Dole").[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-40) In the general election, Pompeo defeated Democratic nominee [Raj Goyle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raj_Goyle "Raj Goyle"), a member of the [Kansas House of Representatives](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas_House_of_Representatives "Kansas House of Representatives"). Pompeo received 59% of the vote (117,171 votes) to 36% for Goyle (71,866).[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-41)

During Pompeo's campaign, its affiliated [Twitter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twitter "Twitter") account praised as a "good read" a news article that called Goyle, his [Indian-American](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian-American "Indian-American") opponent, a "turban topper" who "could be a Muslim, a Hindu, a Buddhist etc. who knows". Pompeo later apologized to Goyle for the tweet.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-42) Pompeo received $80,000 in donations during the campaign from [Koch Industries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Koch_Industries "Koch Industries") and its employees.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-43)

In the [2012 election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_House_of_Representatives_elections_in_Kansas,_2012#District_4 "United States House of Representatives elections in Kansas, 2012"), Pompeo defeated Democratic nominee Robert Tillman by a margin of 62–32%.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-44) Koch Industries gave Pompeo's campaign $110,000.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-nation18-45)

In the [2014 election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_House_of_Representatives_elections_in_Kansas,_2014#District_4 "United States House of Representatives elections in Kansas, 2014"), Pompeo won the general election with 67% of the vote, defeating Democrat Perry Schuckman.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-46)

In the [2016 election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_House_of_Representatives_elections_in_Kansas,_2016#District_4 "United States House of Representatives elections in Kansas, 2016"), Pompeo beat Democrat Daniel B. Giroux in the general election with 61% of the vote.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-47)

### Tenure in Congress

Pompeo served on the [United States House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_House_Permanent_Select_Committee_on_Intelligence "United States House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence"), the [United States House Committee on Energy and Commerce](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_House_Committee_on_Energy_and_Commerce "United States House Committee on Energy and Commerce"), the [United States House Energy Subcommittee on Digital Commerce and Consumer Protection](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_House_Energy_Subcommittee_on_Digital_Commerce_and_Consumer_Protection "United States House Energy Subcommittee on Digital Commerce and Consumer Protection"), the [United States House Energy Subcommittee on Energy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_House_Energy_Subcommittee_on_Energy "United States House Energy Subcommittee on Energy"), the [United States House Intelligence Subcommittee on the CIA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_House_Intelligence_Subcommittee_on_the_CIA "United States House Intelligence Subcommittee on the CIA"), and the [United States House Select Committee on Benghazi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_House_Select_Committee_on_Benghazi "United States House Select Committee on Benghazi").[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-48)

Pompeo was a member of the [Congressional Constitution Caucus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Congressional_Constitution_Caucus "Congressional Constitution Caucus").[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-49)

Pompeo was original sponsor of the [Safe and Accurate Food Labeling Act of 2015](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Safe_and_Accurate_Food_Labeling_Act_of_2015 "Safe and Accurate Food Labeling Act of 2015").[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-gthr-50)

## CIA Director (2017–2018)

[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/11/Mike_Pompeo_official_CIA_portrait.jpg/250px-Mike_Pompeo_official_CIA_portrait.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Mike_Pompeo_official_CIA_portrait.jpg)Official portrait of Mike Pompeo as [CIA Director](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Director_of_the_Central_Intelligence_Agency "Director of the Central Intelligence Agency"), 2017[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/43/CJCS_Arrives_in_France_170713-D-PB383-018.jpg/250px-CJCS_Arrives_in_France_170713-D-PB383-018.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:CJCS_Arrives_in_France_170713-D-PB383-018.jpg)World War II veterans being honored at [Bastille Day](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bastille_Day "Bastille Day") celebrations on July 13, 2017

On November 18, 2016, President-elect [Donald Trump](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donald_Trump "Donald Trump") announced that he would nominate Pompeo to be the [director of the Central Intelligence Agency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Director_of_the_Central_Intelligence_Agency "Director of the Central Intelligence Agency").[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-51) He was confirmed by the Senate on January 23, 2017, with a vote of 66–32, and sworn in later that day.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-52)[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-53) In his confirmation he failed to disclose the links between his company in Kansas and a Chinese government-owned firm.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-54)

In February 2017, Pompeo traveled to [Turkey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turkey "Turkey") and [Saudi Arabia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saudi_Arabia "Saudi Arabia"). He met with Turkish president [Recep Tayyip Erdoğan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Recep_Tayyip_Erdoğan "Recep Tayyip Erdoğan") to discuss policy on Syria and [ISIL](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Islamic_State "Islamic State").[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-55) Pompeo honored the then-[crown prince of Saudi Arabia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crown_Prince_of_Saudi_Arabia "Crown Prince of Saudi Arabia") [Muhammad bin Nayef](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Muhammad_bin_Nayef "Muhammad bin Nayef") with the CIA's "[George Tenet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Tenet "George Tenet")" Medal.[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-56) It was the first reaffirmation of [Saudi Arabia–United States relations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saudi_Arabia–United_States_relations "Saudi Arabia–United States relations") since Trump took office in January 2017.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-57) In March 2017, Pompeo formally invoked [state secrets privilege](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/State_secrets_privilege "State secrets privilege") to prevent CIA officers, including [Gina Haspel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gina_Haspel "Gina Haspel") and [James Cotsana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Cotsana "James Cotsana"), from being compelled to testify in the trial of [Bruce Jessen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bruce_Jessen "Bruce Jessen") and [James Elmer Mitchell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Elmer_Mitchell "James Elmer Mitchell").[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-58)

On 13 April 2017, in an address at the [Center for Strategic and International Studies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Center_for_Strategic_and_International_Studies "Center for Strategic and International Studies"), Pompeo described [WikiLeaks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WikiLeaks "WikiLeaks") as a "hostile intelligence service." This was in response to the publication of [Vault 7](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vault_7 "Vault 7"), that detailed the [electronic surveillance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Surveillance "Surveillance") and [cyber warfare](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cyber_warfare "Cyber warfare") capabilities of the CIA.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-59)

In June 2017, Pompeo named [Michael D'Andrea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_D'Andrea "Michael D'Andrea") head of the CIA's [Iran mission center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iran_Mission_Center "Iran Mission Center").[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-60)

In August 2017, Pompeo took direct command of the Counterintelligence Mission Center, the department which had helped to launch an investigation into possible [links between Trump associates and Russian officials](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Links_between_Trump_associates_and_Russian_officials "Links between Trump associates and Russian officials").[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-ardent-61) Former CIA officials, including [John Sipher](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Sipher "John Sipher"), expressed concern given Pompeo's proximity to the White House and Donald Trump.[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-62)

In September 2017, Pompeo sought authority for the CIA to make covert drone strikes without the [Pentagon's involvement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disposition_Matrix "Disposition Matrix"), including inside Afghanistan.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-63) During [Easter weekend](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Easter "Easter") 2018, Pompeo visited North Korea and met with Supreme Leader [Kim Jong-un](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kim_Jong-un "Kim Jong-un") to discuss the upcoming [2018 North Korea–United States summit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_North_Korea–United_States_Singapore_Summit "2018 North Korea–United States Singapore Summit") between Kim and Trump.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-64)

Pompeo usually personally delivered the [president's daily brief](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President's_Daily_Brief "President's Daily Brief") in the [Oval Office](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oval_Office "Oval Office").[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-65) At Trump's request, Pompeo met with former NSA official [William E. Binney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Binney_(intelligence_official) "William Binney (intelligence official)") to discuss his doubts of [Russian interference in the 2016 United States elections](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russian_interference_in_the_2016_United_States_elections "Russian interference in the 2016 United States elections").[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-NYT14march18-66)

At the suggestion of [Tony Perkins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Perkins_(politician) "Tony Perkins (politician)"), president of the [Family Research Council](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Family_Research_Council "Family Research Council"), Pompeo planned to hire chaplains at the CIA.[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-NYT14march18-66) In an April 2019 speech at Texas A&M University, Pompeo said "I was the CIA director. We lied, we cheated, we stole. It was like we had entire training courses . . . it reminds you of the glory of the American experiment."[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-Newsweek2019-67)[*[better source needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Verifiability#Questionable_sources "Wikipedia:Verifiability")*]

## Secretary of State (2018–2021)

Main article: [Foreign policy of the first Trump administration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Foreign_policy_of_the_first_Trump_administration "Foreign policy of the first Trump administration")

### Nomination and confirmation

President Trump announced on March 13, 2018, that he would nominate Pompeo to serve as [secretary of state](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Secretary_of_State "United States Secretary of State"), succeeding [Rex Tillerson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rex_Tillerson "Rex Tillerson"), who stepped down on March 31, 2018.

[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/7f/Secretary_Pompeo_Meets_with_President_of_Uzbekistan_Shavkat_Mirziyoyev_%2842129787772%29.jpg/250px-Secretary_Pompeo_Meets_with_President_of_Uzbekistan_Shavkat_Mirziyoyev_%2842129787772%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Secretary_Pompeo_Meets_with_President_of_Uzbekistan_Shavkat_Mirziyoyev_(42129787772).jpg)Pompeo with Uzbekistan's president [Shavkat Mirziyoyev](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shavkat_Mirziyoyev "Shavkat Mirziyoyev"), shortly after becoming secretary of state

On April 23, the [Senate Foreign Relations Committee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Senate_Committee_on_Foreign_Relations "United States Senate Committee on Foreign Relations") voted 11–9 in favor of sending Pompeo's nomination to the full Senate, with Senator [Chris Coons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Coons "Chris Coons") voting "present" and [Johnny Isakson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johnny_Isakson "Johnny Isakson"), who was absent that day, voting "yes by proxy".[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-68) In the interest of saving the committee's time, Coons decided to vote "present", as the vote would have been tied if he had voted no on the nomination with Isakson absent, a situation that would have nullified his vote.[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-69) The Senate floor vote took place on April 26 and Pompeo was confirmed by the full Senate by a 57–42 vote, with five of ten Democratic senators running for reelection in [the 2018 midterms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_United_States_Senate_elections "2018 United States Senate elections") in states that Trump won in [2016](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_United_States_presidential_election "2016 United States presidential election"), voting to confirm Pompeo.[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-70)[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-71)[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-off-72)

Pompeo was sworn in on April 26, 2018.[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-off-72) In testimony before the Senate, he promised to prioritize improving the low-morale issue at the State Department.[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-off-72)

### Tenure

See also: [List of international trips made by Mike Pompeo as United States Secretary of State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_international_trips_made_by_Mike_Pompeo_as_United_States_Secretary_of_State "List of international trips made by Mike Pompeo as United States Secretary of State")

[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/02/Secretary_Pompeo_and_Chairman_Kim_Attend_Working_Lunch_in_Pyongyang_%2844430203414%29.jpg/250px-Secretary_Pompeo_and_Chairman_Kim_Attend_Working_Lunch_in_Pyongyang_%2844430203414%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Secretary_Pompeo_and_Chairman_Kim_Attend_Working_Lunch_in_Pyongyang_(44430203414).jpg)Pompeo and North Korean leader [Kim Jong Un](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kim_Jong-un "Kim Jong-un") met in Pyongyang, October 2018.

During his tenure as secretary of state, Pompeo was described as among the staunchest Trump loyalists in the Cabinet.[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-:13-73) During his tenure, he routinely flouted norms followed by his predecessors.[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-:13-73) These included a speech via satellite from Jerusalem supporting Trump's re-election, firing State Department [inspector general](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Office_of_inspector_general_(United_States) "Office of inspector general (United States)") [Steve Linick](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Linick "Steve Linick"), and standing on the sidelines while Trump and his allies conducted a smear campaign against career diplomat [Marie Yovanovitch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marie_Yovanovitch "Marie Yovanovitch").[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-74)[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-:13-73)[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-75)[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-76) Under Pompeo's tenure, career State Department officials quit, were forced into retirement or fired, and were replaced by inexperienced political appointees.[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-:14-77) Like Trump, Pompeo praised dictators and criticized the U.S.'s traditional democratic allies.[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-:13-73)[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-:14-77) International relations scholars [Daniel Drezner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daniel_Drezner "Daniel Drezner"), Richard Sokolsky, and [Aaron David Miller](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_David_Miller "Aaron David Miller") described Pompeo as the worst secretary of state in American history, citing numerous foreign policy failures, fealty to Trump at the cost of U.S. national interest, and improprieties in office.[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-78)[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-79)

Pompeo played a role in Trump's three summits with [North Korean supreme leader](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Supreme_Leader_(North_Korean_title) "Supreme Leader (North Korean title)") [Kim Jong Un](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kim_Jong_Un "Kim Jong Un"). The summits failed to achieve any reduction in [North Korea's nuclear arsenal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_Korea_and_weapons_of_mass_destruction "North Korea and weapons of mass destruction").[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-KellyNK-80)[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-81) In a 2021 interview with a conservative podcast, Pompeo said that "I regret that we didn't make more progress" on North Korea.[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-KellyNK-80)

In August 2018, Pompeo thanked Crown Prince [Mohammad bin Salman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mohammad_bin_Salman "Mohammad bin Salman") "for Saudi Arabia's support for northeast Syria's urgent stabilization needs".[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-82) Pompeo and Crown Prince also discussed the situation in war-torn [Yemen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yemen "Yemen").[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-83)

[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/01/Secretary_Pompeo_Meets_with_Israeli_Prime_Minister_Netanyahu_%2826909878457%29.jpg/250px-Secretary_Pompeo_Meets_with_Israeli_Prime_Minister_Netanyahu_%2826909878457%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Secretary_Pompeo_Meets_with_Israeli_Prime_Minister_Netanyahu_(26909878457).jpg)Pompeo with Israeli prime minister [Benjamin Netanyahu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benjamin_Netanyahu "Benjamin Netanyahu") in April 2018

Pompeo condemned the [military crackdown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rohingya_persecution_in_Myanmar_(2016–present) "Rohingya persecution in Myanmar (2016–present)") by the [Myanmar Army](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Myanmar_Army "Myanmar Army") and police on [Rohingya Muslims](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rohingya_people "Rohingya people").[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-84) In July 2018, Pompeo raised the issue of [Xinjiang internment camps](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xinjiang_internment_camps "Xinjiang internment camps") and human rights abuses against the [Uyghur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uyghurs "Uyghurs") minority in China.[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-85) Pompeo criticized [Iran](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iran "Iran")'s [supreme leader](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Supreme_Leader_of_Iran "Supreme Leader of Iran") Ayatollah [Ali Khamenei](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ali_Khamenei "Ali Khamenei") for his refusal to condemn the Chinese government's repressions against the Uyghurs.[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-86)

On October 10, 2018, Pompeo said [Israel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel "Israel") "is everything we want the entire Middle East to look like going forward" and that the [Israel–United States relations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel–United_States_relations "Israel–United States relations") are "stronger than ever".[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-87) In March 2019, when questioned regarding Israel's conflicts with Iran and following a visit to the Western Wall with Israeli prime minister [Benjamin Netanyahu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benjamin_Netanyahu "Benjamin Netanyahu"), Pompeo spoke to "the work that our administration's done to make sure that this democracy in the Middle East, that this Jewish state, remains ... I am confident that the Lord is at work here."[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-88)

[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/4e/Secretary_Pompeo_Meets_With_Canadian_Prime_Minister_Trudeau_%2848603638792%29.jpg/250px-Secretary_Pompeo_Meets_With_Canadian_Prime_Minister_Trudeau_%2848603638792%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Secretary_Pompeo_Meets_With_Canadian_Prime_Minister_Trudeau_(48603638792).jpg)Pompeo with Canadian prime minister [Justin Trudeau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Trudeau "Justin Trudeau") in August 2019[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/47/Secretary_Pompeo_Meets_With_Polish_Foreign_Minister_Czaputowicz_-_40109273863.jpg/250px-Secretary_Pompeo_Meets_With_Polish_Foreign_Minister_Czaputowicz_-_40109273863.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Secretary_Pompeo_Meets_With_Polish_Foreign_Minister_Czaputowicz_-_40109273863.jpg)Pompeo meeting with Polish foreign minister [Jacek Czaputowicz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jacek_Czaputowicz "Jacek Czaputowicz") in February 2019

On November 16, 2018, a CIA assessment was leaked to the media,[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-89) that concluded with "high confidence" [Saudi Arabia's crown prince](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crown_Prince_of_Saudi_Arabia "Crown Prince of Saudi Arabia") [Mohammad bin Salman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mohammad_bin_Salman "Mohammad bin Salman") ordered the October 2, 2018, assassination of *[Washington Post](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Washington_Post "The Washington Post")* columnist [Jamal Khashoggi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamal_Khashoggi "Jamal Khashoggi").[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-book-90) Under mounting pressure from lawmakers who wanted action against Saudi Arabia, Pompeo disputed the CIA's conclusion and declared there was no direct evidence linking the Crown Prince to the Khashoggi's assassination.[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-book-90)[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-91)

In what was seen as an effort to promote his presumed candidacy in the 2024 Republican presidential primary, Pompeo's book, *[Never Give an Inch: Fighting for the America I Love](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Never_Give_an_Inch:_Fighting_for_the_America_I_Love "Never Give an Inch: Fighting for the America I Love")*, returned to his theme that the assassination and dismemberment was of little international consequence, that the victim was not a reporter of much, if any consequence, and was merely an "activist." He further denigrated Khashoggi as, "...cozy with the terrorist-supporting [Muslim Brotherhood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Muslim_Brotherhood "Muslim Brotherhood")."[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-book-90)

[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/2c/Vladimir_Putin_and_Mike_Pompeo_%282019-05-14%29_02.jpg/250px-Vladimir_Putin_and_Mike_Pompeo_%282019-05-14%29_02.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Vladimir_Putin_and_Mike_Pompeo_(2019-05-14)_02.jpg)Pompeo and Russian president [Vladimir Putin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vladimir_Putin "Vladimir Putin") met in Sochi, May 2019.

On January 7, 2019, Pompeo began a diplomatic tour of the Middle East to assure regional U.S. partners that, amid the [sudden withdrawal of U.S. troops from Syria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American-led_intervention_in_the_Syrian_Civil_War#December_2018 "American-led intervention in the Syrian Civil War"), the U.S. mission to degrade and destroy the [Islamic State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Islamic_State_of_Iraq_and_the_Levant "Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant") and to counter Iranian influence in the region had not changed. The trip included stops in [Jordan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jordan "Jordan"), [Iraq](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iraq "Iraq"), [Egypt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Egypt "Egypt"), and the [Gulf nations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arab_states_of_the_Persian_Gulf "Arab states of the Persian Gulf").[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-92)

Pompeo announced on January 23, 2019, that [Juan Guaidó](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juan_Guaidó "Juan Guaidó") would be recognized by the U.S. as the legitimate interim [president of Venezuela](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_Venezuela "President of Venezuela"), and that American diplomats in [Caracas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caracas "Caracas") would remain at their posts, even as [Nicolás Maduro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nicolás_Maduro "Nicolás Maduro") gave them three days to evacuate the country upon Guaidó assumption of the presidency.[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-93) After protests for over "homophobic, racist and misogynist remarks" by Brazilian president [Jair Bolsonaro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jair_Bolsonaro "Jair Bolsonaro"), a ceremony hosted by the Brazilian-American Chamber of Commerce (originally set to honor Pompeo and Bolsonaro) was canceled.[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-94)

On May 14, 2019, Pompeo met for three hours with Russian foreign minister [Sergey Lavrov](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergey_Lavrov "Sergey Lavrov") and for ninety minutes with Russian president [Vladimir Putin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vladimir_Putin "Vladimir Putin") in [Sochi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sochi "Sochi"), Russia. According to a Kremlin aide, they discussed Syria, North Korea, Iran, Venezuela, and the New Strategic Arms Reduction Treaty ([New START](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_START "New START")); Pompeo said he brought up—and Putin again denied—Russian election interference.[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-issues-95)

In October 2019, the State Department web site promoted a speech by Pompeo "On Being a Christian Leader", which he delivered to the [American Association of Christian Counselors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Association_of_Christian_Counselors "American Association of Christian Counselors") in his official government role. Pompeo touts Christianity in his speech, describes how he applies his faith to his government work. The promotion of the speech by the State Department was met with criticism from those who believed it was incompatible with [separation of church and state](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Separation_of_church_and_state_in_the_United_States "Separation of church and state in the United States").[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-96)[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-97)[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-98) He also created the Commission on Unalienable Rights, and created a faith-based employee affinity group that includes contractors.[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-99)

Pompeo defended the [2019 Turkish offensive into north-eastern Syria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_Turkish_offensive_into_north-eastern_Syria "2019 Turkish offensive into north-eastern Syria"), saying [Turkey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turkey "Turkey") has a "legitimate security concern" with "a terrorist threat to their south".
