#### Madison dinners

From the time he took office in April 2018 until spring 2020, Pompeo had hosted about two dozen taxpayer-funded "Madison dinners" at the [Diplomatic Reception Rooms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diplomatic_Reception_Rooms,_U.S._Department_of_State "Diplomatic Reception Rooms, U.S. Department of State") in the [State Department's headquarters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harry_S_Truman_Building "Harry S Truman Building")) for hundreds of elite attendees.[[120]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-:3-120)[[121]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-Toosi-121) The dinners were not mentioned on Pompeo's public schedule. 14% of the invitees were diplomats or foreign officials while approximately 25% were from—mostly conservative—media or the entertainment industry, 29% from the corporate world, and 30% from U.S. politics or government. Every invited congressional member was a Republican.[[120]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-:3-120) State Department officials and others raised concerns that the dinners did not serve any foreign policy purpose but were intended for Pompeo to cultivate supporters and donors for future political ambitions, especially since detailed contact information for each attendee was sent to Pompeo's wife's personal email address.[[120]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-:3-120)[[121]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-Toosi-121) Pompeo temporarily suspended the "Madison dinners" when the [COVID-19 pandemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_the_United_States "COVID-19 pandemic in the United States") hit the U.S., but resumed the dinners at the [Blair House](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blair_House "Blair House") in September 2020, despite the controversy over them and concerns about public health.[[121]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-Toosi-121)

Records obtained by the watchdog group [Citizens for Responsibility and Ethics in Washington](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Citizens_for_Responsibility_and_Ethics_in_Washington "Citizens for Responsibility and Ethics in Washington") (CREW) in 2021 through a [Freedom of Information Act](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Freedom_of_Information_Act_(United_States) "Freedom of Information Act (United States)") (FOIA) lawsuit revealed that the dinners had cost almost $65,000, including more than $10,000 for custom-engraved, Chinese-made pens given as gifts to the attendees. The funds for the dinners were taken from a special appropriation fund for emergencies in the diplomatic service called the K Fund. The Office of the inspector general told CREW that it had not conducted an audit of K Fund expenditures during Pompeo's tenure.[[122]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-122)[[123]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-123)

#### Threatening of the International Criminal Court

On March 17, 2020, Pompeo threatened two staff members of the [International Criminal Court](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Criminal_Court "International Criminal Court") (ICC), [Phakiso Mochochoko](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phakiso_Mochochoko "Phakiso Mochochoko") and ICC prosecutor [Fatou Bensouda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fatou_Bensouda "Fatou Bensouda")'s in their effort to use the ICC to investigate Americans. Pompeo claimed that they were putting Americans at risk, and intimidated them that the US could act against them, as well as other ICC personnel and their families.[[124]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-124)

Initially the ICC decision had given a decision to approve an investigation into US crimes in Afghanistan for the victims in the hope of justice on March 5, 2020.[[125]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-125) Conditions however included restrictions on the issuance of visas on Mike Pompeo´s instruction from the Department of State.

Immediately after the March 5 decision, Pompeo disparaged the court. The ensuing comments against the ICC staffers were even more pointed. These threats were to used to distract from the US´s failure to hold to account perpetrators of torture and other mistreatment in CIA "black sites" throughout Afghanistan, Poland, Romania, and Lithuania where the ICC had the authority to investigate.[[126]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-126)

Executive Order [13928](https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/Executive%20Order%2013928 "wikisource:Executive Order 13928"),

Eventually, sanctions were applied to the ICC´s personnel without giving the specific reasons other than that they were "specially designated nationals" which would have categorized them within same groupings of terrorists and narcotics traffickers. On june 11, 2020, Trump issued executive order Executive Order [13928](https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/Executive%20Order%2013928 "wikisource:Executive Order 13928"), Blocking Property of Certain Persons Associated With the International Criminal Court. In parallel, while this impeded the ICC investigations in Afghanistan and associated "black site" countries where the Americans had allegedly carried out torture. Concurrently the US also opposed ICC scrutiny of potential Israeli crimes against Palestinians as part of an investigation that also looked into abuses carried out by Israel.[[127]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-127)

Eventually these sanctions were repealed by the [Biden administration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_Joe_Biden "Presidency of Joe Biden") though Executive Order [14022](https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/Executive%20Order%2014022 "wikisource:Executive Order 14022"), on April 1, 2021.[[128]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-128)

#### Inspector general investigations

After [Trump fired](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_dismissal_of_inspectors_general "2020 dismissal of inspectors general") the State Department inspector general, [Steve Linick](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Linick "Steve Linick") in May 2020,[[129]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-:4-129) it became known that Linick had begun an investigation into ethics violations by Pompeo and his wife alleged by whistle-blowers.[[130]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-:5-130)[[131]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-:6-131) The investigation continued after his firing, and the review report was released in April 2021. The review had found more than 100 instances of misconduct where Pompeo requested that State Department staff perform personal errands for him and his wife,[[132]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-132) "from booking salon appointments and private dinner reservations to picking up their dog and arranging tours for the Pompeos' political allies."[[133]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-toosi2021-133) The inspector general concluded that the behavior was inconsistent with regulations [[134]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-134)[[133]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-toosi2021-133)[[135]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-135) and "recommended that various divisions at the State Department, such as the Office of the Legal Adviser, update or draft new guidance that establishes or further clarifies the appropriate use of department funds and staffers when it comes to personal tasks."[[133]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-toosi2021-133)[[136]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-136)

The inspector general had also investigated Pompeo's role in the Trump administration's decision to declare an "emergency" to bypass a congressional freeze on [arms sales to Saudi Arabia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017_United_States–Saudi_Arabia_arms_deal "2017 United States–Saudi Arabia arms deal") and the UAE. Prior to his firing, Linick had requested an interview with Pompeo, which Pompeo had declined.[[137]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-SangerNYT-137) After Linick's firing, it was also revealed that he was investigating claims that a top Pompeo aide had failed to report allegations of workplace violence.[[138]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-138) Pompeo denied that he sought to fire Linick in retaliation.[[129]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-:4-129)

#### Impeachment inquiry against Donald Trump

Main article: [Impeachment inquiry against Donald Trump](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Impeachment_inquiry_against_Donald_Trump "Impeachment inquiry against Donald Trump")

Further information: [Trump–Ukraine scandal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trump–Ukraine_scandal "Trump–Ukraine scandal")

When asked about his knowledge of the controversial call made by President Trump on July 25, 2019, to Ukraine's president [Volodymyr Zelenskyy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy "Volodymyr Zelenskyy"), in which Trump solicited assistance in investigating the son of former vice president and presidential candidate [Joe Biden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Biden "Joe Biden"),[[139]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-139) Pompeo initially said he had little knowledge of Trump's call with Zelenskyy since he had not yet read the transcript of the call. It was later confirmed by officials that he himself had been on the call.[[140]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-140)

Pompeo informed the chairmen of the [House Foreign Affairs Committee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/House_Foreign_Affairs_Committee "House Foreign Affairs Committee"), the [House Intelligence Committee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/House_Intelligence_Committee "House Intelligence Committee"), and the [House Oversight Committee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/House_Oversight_Committee "House Oversight Committee") that their subpoenas for documents regarding Trump's communications with the government of Ukraine "can be understood only as an attempt to 'intimidate, bully, and treat improperly, the distinguished professionals of the Department of State'".[[141]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-141) The three chairmen stated on October 1, 2019, "Any effort to intimidate witnesses or prevent them from talking with Congress—including State Department employees—is illegal and will constitute evidence of obstruction of the impeachment inquiry."[[142]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-142)

[William B. Taylor Jr.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_B._Taylor_Jr. "William B. Taylor Jr."), acting ambassador to Ukraine and one of several current and former State Department officials appearing before congressional investigators, testified on October 22, 2019, that the White House was withholding military aid to Ukraine to force cooperation on U.S. domestic political issues, that [Rudy Giuliani](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rudy_Giuliani "Rudy Giuliani") was running a shadow foreign policy effort parallel to official lines in the State Department, that when [John Bolton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Bolton "John Bolton") and others fought the "effort to hijack" the U.S. relationship with Ukraine, Pompeo failed to respond directly to complaints, leaving Taylor to conclude that lack of timely, congressionally approved military aid would leave Ukrainians dying at the hands of Russian-led forces.[[143]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-143)

In his public testimony on November 20, 2019, ambassador to the European Union [Gordon Sondland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gordon_Sondland "Gordon Sondland") noted in his opening statement that [United States Secretary of Energy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Secretary_of_Energy "United States Secretary of Energy") Rick Perry, then-[U.S. ambassador to NATO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Ambassador_to_NATO "U.S. Ambassador to NATO") [Kurt Volker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kurt_Volker "Kurt Volker") and Sondland himself stayed in touch with [Rudy Giuliani](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rudy_Giuliani "Rudy Giuliani") regarding the president's expectation that a public statement should be made by President Zelenskyy committing Ukraine to look into corruption issues, and that Giuliani "specifically mentioned the 2016 election (including the DNC server) and Burisma as two topics of importance to the President". Sondland said they kept the leadership of the NSC and State Department, including Pompeo, informed about their activities, and that as late as September 24, Pompeo was still telling Volker to talk with Giuliani.[[144]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-144)

An October 23, 2019, [Freedom of Information Act](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Freedom_of_Information_Act_(United_States) "Freedom of Information Act (United States)") (FOIA) request by the liberal watchdog group [American Oversight](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Oversight "American Oversight") persuaded a federal judge to give the State Department 30 days to release Ukraine-related records, including communications between Pompeo and President Trump's personal attorney, Rudy Giuliani. On November 22, the State Department released internal emails and documents bolstering Sondland's congressional testimony that Pompeo had participated in Giuliani's activities relating to Ukraine. Pompeo and Giuliani exchanged emails and phone calls in late March 2019, before Ambassador Marie Yovanovitch was recalled from Ukraine. The documents also showed that the State Department had deliberately deceived Congress about the rationale for Marie Yovanovitch's removal as ambassador to Ukraine.[[145]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-details-145)[[146]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-146) Giuliani later admitted he had spoken to Pompeo on the phone in late March 2019 "to relay information he had gathered during his Ukrainian research". Upon Pompeo's request, he then provided him memos of his interviews of two former Ukrainian prosecutors. Giuliani said he later heard that the details of the memos were passed on to the State Department inspector general (IG) and the FBI for investigation.[[145]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-details-145)

On November 26, 2019, Pompeo appeared to grant legitimacy to a [debunked conspiracy theory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conspiracy_theories_related_to_the_Trump–Ukraine_scandal "Conspiracy theories related to the Trump–Ukraine scandal") that Ukraine, rather than or in addition to Russia, was behind [interference in the 2016 United States elections](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russian_interference_in_the_2016_United_States_elections "Russian interference in the 2016 United States elections").[[147]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-:1-147) He had been asked by a reporter "Do you believe that the U.S. and Ukraine should investigate the theory that it was Ukraine and not Russia that hacked the DNC emails in 2016?"[[148]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-:2-148) Pompeo responded "Any time there is information that indicates any country has messed with American elections, we not only have a right but a duty to make sure we chase that down," adding "to protect our elections, America should leave no stone unturned."[[147]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-:1-147)[[148]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-:2-148)

#### COVID-19 pandemic

Pompeo said the U.S. government is trying to determine if the COVID-19 virus emanated from the [Wuhan Institute of Virology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wuhan_Institute_of_Virology "Wuhan Institute of Virology").[[149]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-149)[[150]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-150) On April 23, 2020, Pompeo claimed that China had denied U.S. scientists permission to enter the country, in an effort to ascertain the origin of the current pandemic. He did not give details of any requests for such visits.[[151]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-151) On May 13, 2020, Pompeo made a swift visit to Israel for his first trip overseas since the outbreak of the coronavirus pandemic.[[152]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-152)

During a spike in case and death numbers in the pandemic, Pompeo hosted large indoor holiday parties involving hundreds of guests, as well as alcohol and food. The parties violated public health guidance and were described as superspreader events. They also violated Washington D.C.'s restrictions on sizable indoor gatherings.[[153]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-:11-153) At the same time, the State Department was advising its employees not to have in-person gatherings.[[153]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-:11-153)[[154]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-154) Photos from the event showed attendees not wearing masks consistently.[[155]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-:12-155) In mid-December 2020, hundreds of invitees rejected invitations to go to one of Pompeo's parties.[[155]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-:12-155) A day later, Pompeo cancelled the final holiday party after he had come in contact with a COVID-19 positive individual.[[156]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-156)[[157]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-157)

#### 2019 emergency arms sale

[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/0b/Secretary_Pompeo_Meets_with_Saudi_Crown_Prince_Mohammed_bin_Salman_%2830421982117%29.jpg/250px-Secretary_Pompeo_Meets_with_Saudi_Crown_Prince_Mohammed_bin_Salman_%2830421982117%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Secretary_Pompeo_Meets_with_Saudi_Crown_Prince_Mohammed_bin_Salman_(30421982117).jpg)Pompeo with Saudi crown prince [Mohammad bin Salman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mohammad_bin_Salman "Mohammad bin Salman") in October 2018[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/ce/Secretary_Pompeo_Meets_With_Crown_Prince_Mohammed_bin_Zayed_%2848759132577%29.jpg/250px-Secretary_Pompeo_Meets_With_Crown_Prince_Mohammed_bin_Zayed_%2848759132577%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Secretary_Pompeo_Meets_With_Crown_Prince_Mohammed_bin_Zayed_(48759132577).jpg)Pompeo with Crown Prince [Mohammed bin Zayed Al Nahyan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mohammed_bin_Zayed_Al_Nahyan "Mohammed bin Zayed Al Nahyan") in [Abu Dhabi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abu_Dhabi "Abu Dhabi"), September 2019

In May 2019, Pompeo announced an "emergency" to push through $8.1 billion of arms sales to [Saudi Arabia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saudi_Arabia "Saudi Arabia") and the [United Arab Emirates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Arab_Emirates "United Arab Emirates"), citing Iranian activity in the [Middle East](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Middle_East "Middle East"). This led to widespread congressional opposition, given the [Saudi-led intervention in the Yemeni civil war](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saudi-led_intervention_in_the_Yemeni_civil_war "Saudi-led intervention in the Yemeni civil war") that contributed to a [humanitarian crisis in Yemen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Famine_in_Yemen_(2016–present) "Famine in Yemen (2016–present)"). The emergency arms sale triggered a probe by then-State Department inspector general [Steve Linick](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Linick "Steve Linick"), into the propriety of the arms sale. Pompeo refused to be interviewed by Linick, who was also leading a separate Office of Inspector General (OIG) investigation into whether Pompeo and his wife used official resources for personal business.[[158]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-2020Report-158)

In May 2020, Trump fired Inspector General Linick at Pompeo's recommendation.[[158]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-2020Report-158) The firing was scrutinized by Congress, and in June 2020, Linick testified that [Brian Bulatao](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brian_Bulatao "Brian Bulatao"), a senior State Department appointee and Pompeo ally, attempted to "bully" and improperly pressure him into halting the investigation.[[158]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-2020Report-158)[[159]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-159) [Stephen Akard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Akard "Stephen Akard"), who became acting IG upon Linick's firing, resigned in August 2020.[[158]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-2020Report-158) A week later, OIG issued a report following the investigation into emergency arms sales; the report found that Pompeo did not violate any procedures in declaring the "emergency" but also determined that the State Department had failed to fully consider the humanitarian impact of the arms sale to Saudi Arabia and the UAE, including the Gulf Arab states' use of U.S. bombs in Yemen, killing thousands of civilians.[[158]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-2020Report-158) The State Department leadership, in a statement issued after the OIG report was released, hailed the former finding, but made not mention of the latter finding.[[158]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-2020Report-158)

#### Republican National Convention speech

On August 25, 2020, Pompeo recorded a speech during an official diplomatic visit to [Jerusalem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerusalem "Jerusalem"),[[160]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-160) during the [Republican National Convention](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Republican_National_Convention "2020 Republican National Convention"), in support of the incumbent and Republican presidential nominee [Donald Trump](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donald_Trump "Donald Trump").[[161]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-Gregorian-161) The speech broke precedent, which established that State Department employees and leaders do not speak at political party events.[[161]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-Gregorian-161) Four days before the speech, Pompeo announced a change to longstanding State Department policy to allow the speech, but specified that the change was a special exceptions that applied only to him.[[161]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-Gregorian-161) Pompeo made the change to the department's rule—allowing the Secretary of State to speak to "political party convention when requested by or for the President"—against the advice of the State Department's senior legal advisers.[[161]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-Gregorian-161)

Following the speech, the [House Foreign Affairs Committee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_House_Committee_on_Foreign_Affairs "United States House Committee on Foreign Affairs")'s [Oversight Subcommittee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_House_Foreign_Affairs_Subcommittee_on_Oversight_and_Investigations "United States House Foreign Affairs Subcommittee on Oversight and Investigations") announced an investigation into whether the speech constituted a violation of the [Hatch Act](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hatch_Act_of_1939 "Hatch Act of 1939"), which restricts [executive branch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Executive_branch_of_the_U.S._Government "Executive branch of the U.S. Government") [civil service](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Civil_service "Civil service") employees from participating in certain forms of political activity.[[162]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-:10-162) A spokesperson for Pompeo said that the department was not bearing any of the costs of the speech and that Pompeo spoke in his "personal capacity.[[161]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-Gregorian-161) After the speech, [Eliot Engel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eliot_Engel "Eliot Engel"), chairman of the Foreign Affairs Committee announced that the committee would draft resolution holding Pompeo in [contempt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Contempt_of_Congress "Contempt of Congress"), saying "he has demonstrated alarming disregard for the laws and rules governing his own conduct and for the tools the constitution provides to prevent government corruption."[[163]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-163) The Oversight Subcommittee Chairman, [Joaquin Castro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joaquin_Castro "Joaquin Castro"), said the "likely unprecedented" speech "may also be illegal."[[162]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-:10-162)

The [Office of the Special Counsel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Office_of_Special_Counsel "United States Office of Special Counsel") launched a probe into Pompeo's speech,[[164]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-164) and in November 2021, the Office released a report concluding that Pompeo was one of at least 13 senior Trump administration officials who violated the Hatch Act.[[161]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-Gregorian-161) The office found that Pompeo had known of the Hatch Act's restrictions before giving the speech and had ignored advice from State Department personnel on "how to comply with the Hatch Act when delivering the speech."[[161]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-Gregorian-161)

#### Afghanistan and the Taliban

[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a0/Secretary_Pompeo_Participates_in_a_Security_Shura.jpg/250px-Secretary_Pompeo_Participates_in_a_Security_Shura.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Secretary_Pompeo_Participates_in_a_Security_Shura.jpg)Pompeo with General [Austin S. Miller](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Austin_S._Miller "Austin S. Miller") in [Kabul](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kabul "Kabul") on June 25, 2019

Pompeo was involved in [negotiations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doha_Agreement_(2020) "Doha Agreement (2020)") with the [Taliban](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taliban "Taliban") that set the stage for a U.S. departure from Afghanistan.[[165]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-:15-165) In early 2020, Pompeo touted the Trump administration's agreement with the Taliban that put the U.S. on a trajectory to leave Afghanistan by May 2021.[[165]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-:15-165) The deal required the Afghan government to release 5,000 imprisoned Taliban members. By August 2020, the Afghan government released all but 400 of the prisoners, as these prisoners had been accused of committing major crimes, according to the [Council on Foreign Relations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Council_on_Foreign_Relations "Council on Foreign Relations"). Pompeo urged the Afghan government to release the remaining prisoners to remove "the last obstacle to the start of intra-Afghan negotiations". Within three days, Afghan president [Ashraf Ghani](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashraf_Ghani "Ashraf Ghani") agreed to the release, which was completed the next month.[[166]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-166)[[167]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-167)

#### Final days in office

After [Joe Biden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Biden "Joe Biden") won the [2020 United States presidential election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_United_States_presidential_election "2020 United States presidential election") and Trump refused to concede while making false claims of fraud, Pompeo, when asked whether there would be a "smooth [transition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_presidential_transition "United States presidential transition")" to the Biden administration, responded on November 10, 2020: "There will be a smooth transition to a second Trump administration, all right. We're ready. The world is watching what's taking place here. We're gonna count all the votes. When the process is complete, they'll be electors selected."[[168]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-ny-farrow-168)[[169]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-169)[[170]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-170)

The day after a [pro-Trump mob stormed the U.S. Capitol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_storming_of_the_United_States_Capitol "2021 storming of the United States Capitol") to prevent the [counting of the electoral votes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_United_States_Electoral_College_vote_count "2021 United States Electoral College vote count") (thus formalizing the upcoming presidency of Biden), the State Department told diplomats to affirm Biden's victory.[[171]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-171) On January 8, Pompeo met with Biden's incoming secretary of state [Antony Blinken](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken "Antony Blinken").[[172]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-172) While other Trump Cabinet members resigned or took a low profile after the attack on the Capitol, in which Trump's role was debated, Pompeo remained a vocal defender of Trump, sending a Twitter message that promoted him as a potential [Nobel Peace Prize](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Peace_Prize "Nobel Peace Prize") nominee.[[173]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-BurstActions-173) He urged followers of the State Department's Twitter account to follow his personal account; criticized the news media, and complained about purported "censorship" of conservatives on social media websites.[[173]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-BurstActions-173)

[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b1/Former_Secretary_Pompeo_Waves_to_Employees_Before_Departing_the_Department_of_State_%2850862603108%29.jpg/250px-Former_Secretary_Pompeo_Waves_to_Employees_Before_Departing_the_Department_of_State_%2850862603108%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Former_Secretary_Pompeo_Waves_to_Employees_Before_Departing_the_Department_of_State_(50862603108).jpg)Pompeo departs the Department of State on January 20, 2021.

On January 12, 2021, Pompeo cancelled a planned European trip when European diplomats declined to meet with him.[[174]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-174)

Pompeo made a large number of foreign policy decisions during the [lame duck period](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lame_duck_(politics) "Lame duck (politics)") of the Trump administration in the weeks leading up to the [inauguration of Joe Biden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inauguration_of_Joe_Biden "Inauguration of Joe Biden"), including many likely to be reversed under Biden.[[173]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-BurstActions-173) Pompeo ordered the re-designation of Cuba as a "[state sponsor of terrorism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/State_Sponsors_of_Terrorism_(U.S._list) "State Sponsors of Terrorism (U.S. list)")"[[173]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-BurstActions-173)[[175]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-175) and the designation of the [Houthi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Houthi "Houthi") rebels as a "[foreign terrorist organization](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Foreign_terrorist_organization "Foreign terrorist organization")".[[173]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-BurstActions-173) The latter decision indirectly reduced humanitarian aid to Yemeni people, and it was quickly reversed by the [Biden administration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biden_administration "Biden administration").[[176]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-176)

On January 19, 2021, Pompeo announced that the Department of State had determined that "genocide and crimes against humanity" had been perpetrated by [China](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/China "China") against the [Uyghur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uyghurs "Uyghurs") [Muslims](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Islam_in_China "Islam in China") and other ethnic minorities in [Xinjiang](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xinjiang "Xinjiang").[[177]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-wsj._U.S._says-177)[[178]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-:22-178) The announcement was made on the last full day of the [presidency of Donald Trump](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_presidency_of_Donald_Trump "First presidency of Donald Trump").[[177]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-wsj._U.S._says-177) On January 20, 2021, Pompeo and several other Trump administration officials were [sanctioned by China](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_sanctions "Chinese sanctions"). In a statement, the [Ministry of Foreign Affairs of China](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ministry_of_Foreign_Affairs_of_China "Ministry of Foreign Affairs of China") stated that it had decided to sanction those "who have seriously violated China's sovereignty and who have been mainly responsible for such U.S. moves on China-related issues." The targeted individuals and their immediate family members were banned from entering mainland China, [Hong Kong](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hong_Kong "Hong Kong") and [Macau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Macau "Macau"), and were also restricted from doing business with China either individually or through their companies and institutions.[[179]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-179)[[180]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-180)[[181]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-181)[[182]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-182) President Biden's National Security Council called the sanctions "unproductive and cynical".[[183]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-PompeoSanctioned-183)[[184]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-184)

After Trump's victory in the [2024 election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_United_States_presidential_election "2024 United States presidential election"), he declared that Pompeo and [Nikki Haley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nikki_Haley "Nikki Haley") would "not be invited to join" his next administration.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-:16-9)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-:17-10) According to *[The Wall Street Journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Wall_Street_Journal "The Wall Street Journal")*, [Tucker Carlson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tucker_Carlson "Tucker Carlson") and [Donald Trump Jr.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donald_Trump_Jr. "Donald Trump Jr.") played a key role in blocking Pompeo's return; Carlson argued that Pompeo was a "warmonger".[[197]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-197) On January 22, 2025, President Trump revoked Pompeo's [security detail](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Security_detail "Security detail").[[198]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-198)

Pompeo said that he suspected he was hired because Columbia was "seeking to bring onto campus…someone with a view that is very different than most of the faculty on their staff."[[199]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-199)

In June 2025, *[The Washington Post](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Washington_Post "The Washington Post")*, citing intelligence sources, reported that Iranian operatives came close to assassinating Pompeo during his visit to [Paris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paris "Paris") in 2022.[[200]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-200) According to the report, the operation was part of a broader Iranian campaign to target former senior U.S. officials involved in the 2020 killing of Quds Force commander [Qasem Soleimani](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Qasem_Soleimani "Qasem Soleimani").[[201]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-AllenIran-201) While the plot ultimately failed, sources revealed that Iranian agents had come alarmingly close to executing the plan on European soil.[[202]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-202)

In November 2025, Pompeo joined the advisory board of Ukrainian defence technology company [Fire Point](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fire_Point_(Ukrainian_firm) "Fire Point (Ukrainian firm)") which specializes in the development and production of long-range strike drones.[[203]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-ki-20251117-203)

## Political positions

### Foreign policy

In 2013, Pompeo supported the surveillance programs of the [National Security Agency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Security_Agency "National Security Agency"), referring to the agency's efforts as "good and important work".[[204]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-204) In 2016 Pompeo stated, "Congress should pass a law re-establishing collection of all metadata, and combining it with publicly available financial and lifestyle information into a comprehensive, searchable database. Legal and bureaucratic impediments to surveillance should be removed. That includes Presidential Policy Directive-28, which bestows privacy rights on foreigners and imposes burdensome requirements to justify data collection."[[205]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-205) In March 2017, [WikiLeaks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WikiLeaks "WikiLeaks") began publishing a series of documents known as [Vault 7](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vault_7 "Vault 7"), detailing the CIA's electronic surveillance and cyber warfare activities and capabilities. In an April 2017 speech addressing the [Center for Strategic and International Studies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Center_for_Strategic_and_International_Studies "Center for Strategic and International Studies"), Pompeo called WikiLeaks "a non-state hostile intelligence service" and described its founder, [Julian Assange](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julian_Assange "Julian Assange"), as a "narcissist" and "a fraud—a coward hiding behind a screen".[[206]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-206)[[207]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-207) In 2022 a [lawsuit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kunstler_v._Central_Intelligence_Agency "Kunstler v. Central Intelligence Agency") was filed against Pompeo and other defendants alleging that they have illegally placed Assange and his guests under surveillance.[[208]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-208)[[209]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-209)

[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/1a/Secretary_Pompeo_Meets_with_Qatari_Amir_Tamim_bin_Hamad_al-Thani_%2849599913542%29.jpg/250px-Secretary_Pompeo_Meets_with_Qatari_Amir_Tamim_bin_Hamad_al-Thani_%2849599913542%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Secretary_Pompeo_Meets_with_Qatari_Amir_Tamim_bin_Hamad_al-Thani_(49599913542).jpg)Pompeo with Qatar's emir [Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tamim_bin_Hamad_Al_Thani "Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani") in Doha, [Qatar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Qatar "Qatar"), February 2020[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f7/Secret%C3%A1rio_de_Estado_Michael_Pompeo_participa_da_cerim%C3%B4nia_de_posse_do_Presidente_Bolsonaro_%2844751487210%29.jpg/250px-Secret%C3%A1rio_de_Estado_Michael_Pompeo_participa_da_cerim%C3%B4nia_de_posse_do_Presidente_Bolsonaro_%2844751487210%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Secretário_de_Estado_Michael_Pompeo_participa_da_cerimônia_de_posse_do_Presidente_Bolsonaro_(44751487210).jpg)Pompeo with Brazilian president [Jair Bolsonaro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jair_Bolsonaro "Jair Bolsonaro") in January 2019

In a 2013 speech on the House floor, Pompeo said [Muslim](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Muslim "Muslim") leaders who fail to denounce acts of [terrorism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Terrorism "Terrorism") done in the name of Islam are "potentially complicit" in the attacks.[[210]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-210) The [Council on American–Islamic Relations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Council_on_American–Islamic_Relations "Council on American–Islamic Relations") called on him to revise his remarks, calling them "false and irresponsible".[[211]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-211) In 2016, [ACT for America](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ACT_for_America "ACT for America") gave Pompeo a "national security eagle award" for his comments on Islam.[[212]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-nyt7april18-212) Pompeo has been a frequent guest on anti-Muslim activist [Frank Gaffney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frank_Gaffney "Frank Gaffney")'s radio show for the [Center for Security Policy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Center_for_Security_Policy "Center for Security Policy").[[212]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-nyt7april18-212) As a congressman, he cosponsored legislation to add the [Muslim Brotherhood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Muslim_Brotherhood "Muslim Brotherhood") to the [United States State Department list of Foreign Terrorist Organizations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_State_Department_list_of_Foreign_Terrorist_Organizations "United States State Department list of Foreign Terrorist Organizations").[[213]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-213)[[214]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-214)

Pompeo opposed closing the [Guantanamo Bay detention camp](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guantanamo_Bay_detention_camp "Guantanamo Bay detention camp").[[215]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-215) After a 2013 visit to the [prison](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prison "Prison"), he said, of the [prisoners](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prisoner "Prisoner") who were on [hunger strike](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hunger_strike "Hunger strike"), "It looked to me like a lot of them had put on weight."[[216]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-216) He criticized the [Obama administration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Obama_administration "Obama administration")'s decision to end [secret prisons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_site "Black site") and its requirement that all interrogators adhere to anti-[torture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Torture "Torture") laws.[[217]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-217)

In March 2014, he denounced the inclusion of a telecast by [Edward Snowden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Snowden "Edward Snowden") at the [South by Southwest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_by_Southwest "South by Southwest") conference in [Austin, Texas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Austin,_Texas "Austin, Texas"), and asked that it be cancelled, predicting it would encourage "lawless behavior" among attendees.[[218]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-218) In February 2016, Pompeo said Snowden "should be brought back from Russia and given due process, and I think the proper outcome would be that he would be given a death sentence."[[219]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-219) But he has spoken in favor of reforming the [Federal Records Act](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_Records_Act "Federal Records Act"), one of the laws under which Snowden was charged, saying, "I'm not sure there's a whole lot of change that needs to happen to the [Espionage Act](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Espionage_Act "Espionage Act"). The Federal Records Act clearly needs updating to reflect the different ways information is communicated and stored. Given the move in technology and communication methods, I think it's probably due for an update."[[220]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-220)

On July 21, 2015, Pompeo and Senator [Tom Cotton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tom_Cotton "Tom Cotton") alleged the existence of secret side agreements between Iran and the [International Atomic Energy Agency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Atomic_Energy_Agency "International Atomic Energy Agency") (IAEA) on procedures for inspection and verification of Iran's nuclear activities under the Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action. Obama administration officials acknowledged the existence of agreements between Iran and the IAEA governing the inspection of sensitive military sites but denied that they were "secret side deals", calling them standard practice in crafting arms-control pacts and saying the administration had provided information about them to Congress.[[221]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-221)

In November 2015, Pompeo visited [Israel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel "Israel") and said, "Prime Minister [[Benjamin] Netanyahu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benjamin_Netanyahu "Benjamin Netanyahu") is a true partner of the American people."[[222]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-hawkish-222) He supported Trump's 2017 decision to move America's embassy in Israel to Jerusalem.[[223]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-veconomist-223)

In 2017, Pompeo worked to undermine the [Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joint_Comprehensive_Plan_of_Action "Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action") nuclear deal with Iran (which had been negotiated by the Obama administration) saying, "I look forward to rolling back this disastrous deal with the world's largest state sponsor of terrorism."[[224]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-224) He also said a better option than negotiating with Iran would be to use "under 2,000 sorties to destroy the Iranian nuclear capacity. This is not an insurmountable task for the coalition forces."

In 2017, it was reported that Pompeo had expressed desire for regime change in [North Korea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_Korea "North Korea").[[225]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-225) In July 2017, he said "It would be a great thing to denuclearize the peninsula, to get those weapons off of that, but the thing that is most dangerous about it is the character who holds the control over them today."[[226]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-226)

In September 2018, Pompeo "backed continued U.S. military support for [Saudi Arabia's war in Yemen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saudi_Arabian-led_intervention_in_Yemen "Saudi Arabian-led intervention in Yemen") over the objections of staff members after being warned that a cutoff could jeopardize $2 billion in weapons sales to America's Gulf allies, according to a classified memo and people familiar with the decision".[[227]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-227)

In November 2018, Pompeo blamed [Iran](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iran "Iran") for the [humanitarian crisis in Yemen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Famine_in_Yemen_(2016–present) "Famine in Yemen (2016–present)"), saying, "Iran causes death and destruction inside of Yemen and does nothing to prevent the starvation," while Saudi Arabia has "provided millions and millions of dollars of humanitarian relief" for Yemen.[[228]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-228)

**Israel**

Pompeo has consistently expressed strong support for Israel, describing it as a major ally of the United States and an anchor of regional stability. He has advocated for close [US—Israel relations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel–United_States_relations "Israel–United States relations") and supported Israel's security policies. Pompeo has repeatedly affirmed Israel's right to defend itself, condemned [Hamas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hamas "Hamas"), and stressed the importance of maintaining strong deterrence against hostile actors in the Middle East, while criticizing policies he believes undermine Israel' security.[[229]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-229)[[230]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-230) He has also criticized moves by countries such as Britain, Portugal, France, Canada, and Australia to recognize a "so-called Palestinian state" and called it "nothing short of perverse". He contended that such recognition will prolong the suffering of the people of Gaza rather than securing peace in the region. Furthermore, Pompeo has expressed a negative view of the [Boycott Divestment and Sanctions (BDS)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boycott,_Divestment_and_Sanctions "Boycott, Divestment and Sanctions") movement, arguing that is unfairly targets Israel and should be regarded as antisemitic.[[231]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-231)[[232]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-232)

While being interviewed on a podcast in 2023, Pompeo has argued that Israel's long-standing control of the West Bank and Gaza should not be described as an occupation, claiming that Israel has biblical and historical ties to the land. He made several striking statements during the interview, including calling Palestinian president [Mahmoud Abbas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mahmoud_Abbas "Mahmoud Abbas") a "known terrorist".[[233]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-233)

#### China

[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a3/Secretary_Pompeo_Meets_With_Chinese_President_Xi_Jinping_in_Beijing_%2840985611020%29.jpg/250px-Secretary_Pompeo_Meets_With_Chinese_President_Xi_Jinping_in_Beijing_%2840985611020%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Secretary_Pompeo_Meets_With_Chinese_President_Xi_Jinping_in_Beijing_(40985611020).jpg)Pompeo and [Chinese Communist Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_Communist_Party "Chinese Communist Party") general secretary and Chinese president [Xi Jinping](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xi_Jinping "Xi Jinping")

During his tenure as secretary of state, Pompeo was an outspoken critic of China. Pompeo suggested that Chinese investment in Israel would create issues between the U.S. and Israel, and threatened to reduce security arrangements between the countries, although he also claimed that he would have no problems with open and transparent investments.[[234]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-234) He accused the [World Health Organization](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Health_Organization "World Health Organization") of being under control of the [People's Republic of China](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/China "China") and implicated China as being behind the significant number of deaths in the UK as a result of the [COVID-19 pandemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_the_United_Kingdom "COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom").[[235]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-:8-235) He praised the UK when they started to push back against the [Chinese Communist Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Communist_Party_of_China "Communist Party of China") and its [General Secretary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/General_Secretary_of_the_Communist_Party_of_China "General Secretary of the Communist Party of China") [Xi Jinping](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xi_Jinping "Xi Jinping"), especially with respect to [Huawei](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Huawei "Huawei").[[236]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-236) He also said he preferred a new coalition that did not need to go through established institutions that were set up by the United States, such as the United Nations.[[237]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-Bourke-237) He argued that China was a "new tyranny" and it was the duty of "every leader of every nation" to stand up to China.[[238]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-238)

Pompeo has also argued that China's claims and activities in the South China Sea were illegal. In addition he said the Chinese authorities were not allowed to take unilateral action in the area.[[239]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-239) Michael Hirson, at [Eurasia Group](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eurasia_Group "Eurasia Group"), argued that Pompeo was calling for regime change.[[240]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-:9-240) He called on the Chinese people to betray their government and rise up to change the Chinese Communist Party.[[241]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-241)

On July 23, 2020, Pompeo, during his Communist China and the Free World's Future speech, announced the end of what he called "blind engagement" with the Chinese government. He also criticized Chinese Communist Party general secretary Xi Jinping[[242]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-242) as "a true believer in a bankrupt totalitarian ideology".[[243]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-243)

The former assistant secretary of state for East Asian and Pacific affairs, [Daniel Russel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daniel_Russel "Daniel Russel"), argued that it would have "the opposite effect, in bolstering support in China for Xi Jinping and deepening anger towards the United States". Michael Hirson noted that with the [2020 U.S. presidential election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_United_States_presidential_election "2020 United States presidential election") nearing, it was unlikely Chinese policymakers would do anything to change their relationship.[[240]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-:9-240)

In September 2020, Pompeo accused the Chinese government of trying to foment racial unrest in the United States during an address to state lawmakers in Wisconsin.[[244]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-244)

In October 2020, Donald Trump was [diagnosed with COVID-19](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_House_COVID-19_outbreak "White House COVID-19 outbreak"), and Pompeo cancelled scheduled visits to South Korea and Mongolia.[[245]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-245) However, he still held a meeting with the foreign ministers of [Quad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quadrilateral_Security_Dialogue "Quadrilateral Security Dialogue") allies Australia, India and Japan, during which he accused the Chinese Communist Party of "exploitation, corruption and coercion".[[246]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-246)

#### Taiwan

[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/19/05.21_%E7%B8%BD%E7%B5%B1%E6%8E%A5%E8%A6%8B%E3%80%8C%E7%BE%8E%E5%9C%8B%E7%AC%AC_70_%E4%BB%BB%E5%9C%8B%E5%8B%99%E5%8D%BF%E9%BE%90%E5%9F%B9%E6%AD%90%E8%A8%AA%E5%95%8F%E5%9C%98%E3%80%8D.jpg/250px-05.21_%E7%B8%BD%E7%B5%B1%E6%8E%A5%E8%A6%8B%E3%80%8C%E7%BE%8E%E5%9C%8B%E7%AC%AC_70_%E4%BB%BB%E5%9C%8B%E5%8B%99%E5%8D%BF%E9%BE%90%E5%9F%B9%E6%AD%90%E8%A8%AA%E5%95%8F%E5%9C%98%E3%80%8D.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:05.21_總統接見「美國第_70_任國務卿龐培歐訪問團」.jpg)Pompeo with [Taiwanese President](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_the_Republic_of_China "President of the Republic of China") [William Lai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lai_Ching-te "Lai Ching-te") in May 2024. Pompeo supports official U.S. recognition of Taiwan as a sovereign country.

Visiting [Taipei](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taipei "Taipei") in 2022, Pompeo said that the U.S. should recognize the [Republic of China (Taiwan)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taiwan "Taiwan") as an independent country.[[247]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-247) He returned to Taiwan in May 2024, as part of the American delegation to the inauguration of [President](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_the_Republic_of_China "President of the Republic of China") [William Lai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lai_Ching-te "Lai Ching-te"). Pompeo met with Lai the following day, reiterating his support for official U.S. recognition of the country.[[248]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-248)[[249]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-249)

#### Russia

During his confirmation hearing, Pompeo said Russia "has reasserted itself aggressively, invading and occupying Ukraine, threatening Europe, and doing nearly nothing to aid in the destruction and defeat of [ISIS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISIS "ISIS")".[[250]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-250)

In August 2018, Pompeo called Russia to "immediately release" jailed Ukrainian filmmaker [Oleg Sentsov](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oleg_Sentsov "Oleg Sentsov").[[251]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-251)

In February 2022, right before [Russia invaded Ukraine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_Russian_invasion_of_Ukraine "2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine"), Pompeo gave an interview in which he praised Russian president [Vladimir Putin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vladimir_Putin "Vladimir Putin"). Russian state television aired the interview. Pompeo's comments reflected comments made by Trump after the invasion praising Putin.[[252]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-252) The same month, during a speech at the [Conservative Political Action Conference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conservative_Political_Action_Conference "Conservative Political Action Conference"), Pompeo called Putin a "[dictator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dictator "Dictator")" over the invasion, though also stated that he continued to believe that China was a greater national security threat to the United States than Russia.[[253]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-253)

During a speech at the [Hudson Institute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hudson_Institute "Hudson Institute") in June 2022, Pompeo described the Russian invasion of Ukraine as a "planned genocide" designed to create a "new Russian Empire" similar to the [Soviet Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soviet_Union "Soviet Union") with large amounts of energy reserves.[[254]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-254)

### Energy and environment

[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/0e/Mike_Pompeo_by_Gage_Skidmore_2.jpg/250px-Mike_Pompeo_by_Gage_Skidmore_2.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Mike_Pompeo_by_Gage_Skidmore_2.jpg)Pompeo at the [Values Voter Summit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Values_Voter_Summit "Values Voter Summit") in Washington, D.C.

Speaking about climate change in 2013, Pompeo said: "There are scientists who think lots of different things about climate change. There's some who think we're warming, there's some who think we're cooling, there's some who think that the last 16 years have shown a pretty stable climate environment."[[255]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-255) He has said, "Federal policy should be about the American family, not worshipping a radical environmental agenda." In 2009 Pompeo signed the No Climate Tax pledge of Americans for Prosperity.[[256]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-256) He called the Obama administration's environment and climate change plans "damaging" and "radical". In 2012 he called for the permanent elimination of wind power production tax credits, calling them an "enormous government handout".[[257]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-257)

In 2015, Pompeo opposed the regulation of [greenhouse gas emissions by the United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greenhouse_gas_emissions_by_the_United_States "Greenhouse gas emissions by the United States") and supported eliminating the [United States federal register of greenhouse gas emissions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_federal_register_of_greenhouse_gas_emissions "United States federal register of greenhouse gas emissions").[[258]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-cleanair-258) As a member of the United States House Committee on Energy and Commerce, he voted for two resolutions disapproving of the [Clean Power Plan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clean_Power_Plan "Clean Power Plan") implemented by the [United States Environmental Protection Agency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Environmental_Protection_Agency "United States Environmental Protection Agency") during the Obama administration.

In May 2019, Pompeo acted against environmental protection at the Arctic Council. He refused to sign on to a joint statement addressing the need for protection of the Arctic region from the threat of rapidly melting ice unless all mentions of climate change were removed from the document. He said, "Climate change is actually good for the Arctic, since melting ice caps are 'opening up new shipping routes' and thus making it more economically viable to expand oil drilling in the region."[[259]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-259)[[260]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-260)

He described the Paris climate accord, along with the World Health Organization and Human Rights Council, as one of the "three sins".[[237]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-Bourke-237)

### Health care

Pompeo opposed the [Affordable Care Act](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Affordable_Care_Act "Affordable Care Act") (ACA).[[261]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-261) Pompeo has been criticized for saying he supports funding for certain programs, yet opposing them when they are a part of the ACA.[[262]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-262) He accused the [World Health Organization](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Health_Organization "World Health Organization") of being under control of the [People's Republic of China](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/China "China").[[235]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-:8-235) The WHO responded by saying Pompeo's comments were unacceptable and a distraction from dealing with the [coronavirus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coronavirus_disease_2019 "Coronavirus disease 2019") pandemic. Dr. [Maria Van Kerkhove](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maria_Van_Kerkhove "Maria Van Kerkhove"), an American who was head of the WHO's emerging diseases and [zoonosis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zoonosis "Zoonosis") unit at the time of the pandemic also expressed pride at the WHO for "saving lives".[[263]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-263) It was argued that the attempt to blame the WHO was a way to draw attention away from the failings of the Trump administration.[[264]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-264)

### Social issues

[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d8/U.S._Congressman_Mike_Pompeo_speaking_at_Freedomworks_New_Fair_Deal_Rally_outside_the_US_Capitol.jpg/250px-U.S._Congressman_Mike_Pompeo_speaking_at_Freedomworks_New_Fair_Deal_Rally_outside_the_US_Capitol.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:U.S._Congressman_Mike_Pompeo_speaking_at_Freedomworks_New_Fair_Deal_Rally_outside_the_US_Capitol.jpg)Congressman Pompeo at [FreedomWorks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FreedomWorks "FreedomWorks") New Fair Deal rally outside the [U.S. Capitol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Capitol "U.S. Capitol"), April 2013

Pompeo has stated that life begins at conception and believes abortions should be allowed only when necessary to save the life of the mother, with no exceptions for rape.[[265]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-265) In 2011, he voted for the [No Taxpayer Funding for Abortion Act](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/No_Taxpayer_Funding_for_Abortion_Act "No Taxpayer Funding for Abortion Act"), which would have banned federal health coverage that includes abortion. On May 31, 2011, he voted for H.R.2059 11-HR2059, which eliminated funding for the [United Nations Population Fund](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations_Population_Fund "United Nations Population Fund").[[266]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-266)

He opposes [same-sex marriage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage "Same-sex marriage") and sponsored bills to let states prevent same-sex couples from marrying.[[267]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-267)[[268]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-268)

Pompeo was instrumental in the development of the anti-abortion [Geneva Consensus Declaration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geneva_Consensus_Declaration "Geneva Consensus Declaration").[[269]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-Southern2021-269)

### Economy

Pompeo supported the [United States federal government shutdown of 2013](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_federal_government_shutdown_of_2013 "United States federal government shutdown of 2013"), blaming President Obama. He said he believed the shutdown was necessary to avoid an "American financial collapse 10 years from now".[[270]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-270)

### International Criminal Court

Pompeo continued a non-cooperative policy towards the [International Criminal Court](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Criminal_Court "International Criminal Court") in [The Hague](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Hague "The Hague"), enacting sanctions against the ICC's chief prosecutor and other officials in September 2020.[[271]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-271) Some security experts have suggested Pompeo himself could potentially face charges under the ICC statutes for [CIA activities in Afghanistan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CIA_activities_in_Afghanistan "CIA activities in Afghanistan") during his time as director of that agency.[[272]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-272)[[273]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-273)

## Personal life

[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f9/Mike_Pompeo_family.jpg/250px-Mike_Pompeo_family.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Mike_Pompeo_family.jpg)Mike Pompeo (center) with wife Susan and son Nicholas in 2018

Pompeo married Leslie Libert in 1986.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-topcadet-17) The couple later divorced. He then married Susan Justice Mostrous in 2000 and formally adopted her son, Nicholas.[[274]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-:0-274)[[275]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-275)

Pompeo is affiliated with the [Evangelical Presbyterian Church](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evangelical_Presbyterian_Church_(United_States) "Evangelical Presbyterian Church (United States)").[[276]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-276)[[277]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-277) Pompeo served as a local church [deacon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deacon "Deacon") from 2007 to 2009 and taught [Sunday school](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sunday_school "Sunday school").[[278]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-278)

In 2014, Pompeo told a church group that Christians needed to "know that [Jesus Christ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jesus_Christ "Jesus Christ") as our savior is truly the only solution for our world".[[279]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-279) In 2015 in a talk at a church, Pompeo said that "politics is a never-ending struggle ... until the [Rapture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rapture "Rapture")."[[280]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-280)

In an interview with [Fox News](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fox_News "Fox News") in January 2022, Pompeo said he has lost over 90 lb (41 kg) in the prior six months through self-guided exercises and dietary changes. Experts were skeptical of Pompeo's claim that such changes could have produced this weight loss in a man his age, and *[The Guardian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Guardian "The Guardian")* said that Pompeo's history of misleading statements cast further doubt on his claims.[[281]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo#cite_note-281)
