### Republican campaign fundraising and donations

According to [OpenSecrets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/OpenSecrets "OpenSecrets"), Tillerson has made tens of thousands of dollars of political donations to Republican groups and candidates.[[182]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rex_Tillerson#cite_note-ssnbc-182) According to [Federal Election Commission](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_Election_Commission "Federal Election Commission") (FEC) records, he gave a total of $468,970 in contributions to Republican candidates and committees from 2000 to 2016.[[183]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rex_Tillerson#cite_note-183)

He has contributed to the political campaigns of [George W. Bush](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush "George W. Bush"),[[182]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rex_Tillerson#cite_note-ssnbc-182) as well as [Mitt Romney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mitt_Romney "Mitt Romney") in 2012, and [Mitch McConnell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mitch_McConnell "Mitch McConnell").[[184]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rex_Tillerson#cite_note-184) He did not donate to Donald Trump's campaign.[[182]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rex_Tillerson#cite_note-ssnbc-182) He donated to [Jeb Bush](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeb_Bush "Jeb Bush")'s campaign during the [2016 Republican primaries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Republican_Party_presidential_primaries "2016 Republican Party presidential primaries").[[182]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rex_Tillerson#cite_note-ssnbc-182)[[185]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rex_Tillerson#cite_note-185)

## Personal life

[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/57/Secretary_Tillerson_and_Mrs._St._Clair_Walk_Through_the_State_Department%27s_Main_Lobby_on_his_First_Day_%2832516939282%29.jpg/250px-Secretary_Tillerson_and_Mrs._St._Clair_Walk_Through_the_State_Department%27s_Main_Lobby_on_his_First_Day_%2832516939282%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Secretary_Tillerson_and_Mrs._St._Clair_Walk_Through_the_State_Department's_Main_Lobby_on_his_First_Day_(32516939282).jpg)Tillerson and Renda St. Clair walk through the State Department building on his first day as Secretary of State, February 1, 2017

Tillerson has been married twice. He divorced Jamie Lee Henry, his first wife, with whom he has two children.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rex_Tillerson#cite_note-codys-25)[[186]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rex_Tillerson#cite_note-sco-186)[[187]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rex_Tillerson#cite_note-FOOTNOTEColl2012a137-187) In 1986, Tillerson married Renda St. Clair. Tillerson and St. Clair also have a child.[[187]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rex_Tillerson#cite_note-FOOTNOTEColl2012a137-187)[[188]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rex_Tillerson#cite_note-188)

Tillerson resides in [Bartonville, Texas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bartonville,_Texas "Bartonville, Texas").[[189]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rex_Tillerson#cite_note-cand-189) Following his appointment as secretary of state, Tillerson bought a home in [Kalorama, Washington, D.C.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sheridan-Kalorama_Historic_District "Sheridan-Kalorama Historic District")[[190]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rex_Tillerson#cite_note-190)

He is a [Congregationalist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Congregationalist "Congregationalist") who holds a membership in the [National Association of Congregational Christian Churches](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Association_of_Congregational_Christian_Churches "National Association of Congregational Christian Churches"), a [mainline](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mainline_Protestant "Mainline Protestant") [Reformed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reformed_tradition "Reformed tradition") denomination.[[191]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rex_Tillerson#cite_note-191)[[192]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rex_Tillerson#cite_note-FOOTNOTEColl2012a569-192) He and his wife donated between $5,000 and $10,000 to the denomination's *The Congregationalist Magazine* in 2012.[[193]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rex_Tillerson#cite_note-193)[[194]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rex_Tillerson#cite_note-CongregationalistDonor-194)

On February 20, 2014, news outlets reported that Tillerson and his wife had joined opponents of a proposed water tower that could lead to fracking-related traffic near their homes. Plaintiffs included former U.S. House of Representatives Majority Leader [Dick Armey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dick_Armey "Dick Armey") and his wife.[[195]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rex_Tillerson#cite_note-fracking_reuters-195)[[196]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rex_Tillerson#cite_note-fracking_wsj-196) The Tillersons dropped out of the lawsuit after a judge dismissed their claim in November 2014.[[197]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rex_Tillerson#cite_note-197)

On May 16, 2018, Tillerson gave a graduation speech at [Virginia Military Institute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virginia_Military_Institute "Virginia Military Institute"). In an apparent rebuke of President Trump, Tillerson warned that there is "a growing crisis in ethics and integrity".[[198]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rex_Tillerson#cite_note-198) "If our leaders seek to conceal the truth or we as people become accepting of alternative realities that are no longer grounded in facts, then we as American citizens are on a pathway to relinquishing our freedom."[[199]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rex_Tillerson#cite_note-199)
